items.title: GitVersioned
items.text:
One version for the whole repository, from git tags. gitversioned resolves it, stamps it into every Python, Rust, npm, Helm and container manifest, checks Conventional Commit titles and drives a reviewed release with a changelog. Three commands: version, check and release.

Get Started View on GitHub

items.title: Overview
items.text:
Every step of a version's life is one command, and the same engine runs inside the build backends.

When Command Every Python build none: the Hatchling, setuptools or Maturin hook Print the version in a script gitversioned version Stamp every manifest before a build gitversioned version --write Nightly build gitversioned version --type nightly --write What the next release would be, and why gitversioned version --next --explain Is this repository set up correctly gitversioned check Pull request title check gitversioned check "$PR_TITLE" Preview a release gitversioned release Open or refresh the release pull request gitversioned release --pr Tag the merged release gitversioned release --tag

• Python 3.10 or newer
  • git on the PATH

items.title: As a command line tool

# Run without installing
uvx gitversioned version
pipx run gitversioned version

# Or install it
uv tool install gitversioned
pipx install gitversioned
pip install gitversioned

items.title: Verify the installation
items.text:
$ gitversioned --version
gitversioned v0.4.0
$ gitversioned check

gitversioned check reports whether the repository can give a trustworthy version and lists the files that would be stamped.

items.title: As a build dependency
items.text:
A Python project does not install gitversioned by hand. It lists it in build-system.requires and the build front end installs it into the isolated build:

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling", "gitversioned>=0.4"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

See the Hatchling, Setuptools and Maturin guides.

items.title: Container image
items.text:
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo" -w /repo ghcr.io/markurtz/git-versioned:latest \
  gitversioned version

items.title: From source
items.text:
git clone https://github.com/markurtz/git-versioned.git
cd git-versioned
uv sync
uv run gitversioned --version

items.text:
uv tool upgrade gitversioned     # or: pipx upgrade gitversioned
uv tool uninstall gitversioned   # or: pipx uninstall gitversioned

Upgrading from 0.3? See the Migration Guide.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Fix The version is 0.1.0... in CI, or exit code 3 The clone is shallow. Set fetch-depth: 0 on actions/checkout. A GitHub source tarball builds as 0.1.0 Run gitversioned init once and commit the two files. settings found in two homes Keep the settings in one file. release --pr says gh is missing Install the GitHub CLI and set GH_TOKEN in CI.

items.title: Quick Start
items.text: Five minutes from an empty repository to a planned release.

items.title: 1. Print the version
items.text:
$ cd my-project
$ uvx gitversioned version
0.1.0.dev20261125+abc1234

With no tags yet the version starts from the fallback 0.1.0. Tag a release and it follows the tag:

$ git tag v1.0.0
$ gitversioned version
1.0.0

items.title: 2. Check the setup
items.text:
$ gitversioned check
ok    config        defaults
ok    git           full history, 1 release tags, latest v1.0.0
ok    targets       Cargo.toml, package.json, src/my_project/version.py
warn  archive file  .git_archival.txt is not set up, so source tarballs lose the version. Run `gitversioned init`.

The targets line lists every file gitversioned found a version in. Run gitversioned init once to clear the archive warning.

items.title: 3. Wire up the build
items.text:
For a Python project, let the build read the version from git:

# pyproject.toml
[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling", "gitversioned>=0.4"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "my-project"
dynamic = ["version"]

[tool.hatch.version]
source = "gitversioned"

[tool.hatch.build.hooks.gitversioned]

For Rust, npm, Helm and container builds, stamp the manifests before building:

$ gitversioned version --write
1.0.1.dev20261125+abc1234
  Cargo.toml    1.0.1-dev.20261125+abc1234
  package.json  1.0.1-dev.20261125+abc1234

items.title: 4. Commit with Conventional Commits
items.text:
$ git commit -m "feat(core): add streaming parser"
$ git commit -m "fix(cli): exit code on empty input"
$ gitversioned check --commits v1.0.0..HEAD
ok    commits  2 commits

items.title: 5. Plan the release
items.text:
$ gitversioned release
release   1.1.0  (minor, from commits, from 1.0.0)
tag       v1.1.0
files     CHANGELOG.md, Cargo.toml, package.json

## 1.1.0 - 2026-11-25

### Added

- **core**: add streaming parser

### Fixed

- **cli**: exit code on empty input

Nothing changed. Run with --write, --pr or --tag.

gitversioned release --pr opens the release pull request with exactly that content. After it merges, gitversioned release --tag tags the merge.

items.title: Workflows
items.text: The common stories, end to end.

items.title: A build that always has the right version
items.text:
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0
- run: pipx run build

With gitversioned in build-system.requires, a tag build is 1.2.0 and every other build is a development version such as 1.2.1.dev20261125+abc1234.

items.title: Every manifest in step
items.text:
gitversioned version --write
cargo build --release --locked
npm pack
docker build --build-arg VERSION="$(gitversioned version --standard semver)" .

One command stamps Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, package.json, Chart.yaml, CITATION.cff and the Dockerfile label, each in its own spelling.

items.title: A reviewed release
items.text:
1. Pull requests merge to main with Conventional Commit titles, checked by gitversioned check "$TITLE".
  2. On every push to main, gitversioned release --pr opens or updates the release pull request: the changelog section and the stamped manifests.
  3. A maintainer reviews, edits the changelog if needed and merges.
  4. gitversioned release --tag tags the merge, and the tag starts the publish jobs.

The full workflow files are in the GitHub Workflows Guide.

items.title: A release candidate
items.text: Add the label release:rc to the release pull request. It becomes release: v1.5.0-rc.1; each further merge and tag gives rc.2, rc.3. Remove the label to release 1.5.0, whose changelog section replaces the candidates'.

items.title: Nightly builds
items.text:
gitversioned version --write --type nightly
python -m build

A nightly is the next release with the date, such as 1.5.0.dev20261125, and has no commit hash, so package indexes accept it.

items.title: One package of a monorepo
items.text:
[packages.web]
path = "packages/web"
tag = "web-v{version}"

gitversioned version -p web
gitversioned release -p web --pr

The package is versioned from its own tags and only the commits that touch its folder count.

items.title: Python API Guide
items.text:
Everything the command line does is available from Python. The top-level package exports the stable surface.

Name What it is get_version(root, standard=) The version of a project as text. load_config(start) The validated settings for a project. resolve(config, ...) The resolved version with its source, tag and commit. stamp(config, resolved, ...) Write the version into every target. plan_release(config, ...) The next release: version, tag, changelog section. Version A version that prints as PEP 440 or SemVer. GitVersionedError and subclasses Errors, each with the exit code the CLI would use.

items.title: Get the version
items.text:
from gitversioned import get_version

print(get_version())  # 1.4.1.dev20261125+60439dc
print(get_version(standard="semver"))  # 1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc
print(get_version("path/to/project"))

items.title: Resolve with detail
items.text:
from gitversioned import load_config, resolve

config = load_config()
resolved = resolve(config)

print(resolved.version.pep440())  # 1.4.1.dev20261125+60439dc
print(resolved.type)  # dev, nightly or release
print(resolved.source)  # tag, archive, metadata, pin or fallback
print(resolved.tag, resolved.distance, resolved.sha)
print(resolved.warnings)

nightly = resolve(config, build_type="nightly")
pinned = resolve(config, pin="2.0.0")

items.title: Stamp files
items.text:
from gitversioned import load_config, resolve, stamp

config = load_config()
for change in stamp(config, resolve(config), dry_run=True):
    print(change.path, change.old, "->", change.new)

Each Change has path, old, new, diff, commit and written.

items.title: Plan a release
items.text:
from gitversioned import NothingToReleaseError, load_config, plan_release

try:
    plan = plan_release(load_config(), use_github=False)
except NothingToReleaseError:
    print("nothing to release")
else:
    print(plan.version.pep440(), plan.tag, plan.level)
    print(plan.section)  # the changelog section, as Markdown

items.title: Work with versions
items.text:
Version needs no repository, so it is useful on its own for parsing, comparing and converting.

from gitversioned import Version

version = Version.parse("1.2.0-rc.1")
print(version.pep440())
print(version.semver())
print(version.is_final)
print(version.bump("minor").pep440())
print(Version.try_parse("not a version"))

names = ["1.2.0", "1.2.0rc1", "1.2.0.dev1", "1.1.9"]
print(sorted(names, key=lambda name: Version.parse(name).sort_key()))

1.2.0rc1
1.2.0-rc.1
False
1.3.0
None
['1.1.9', '1.2.0.dev1', '1.2.0rc1', '1.2.0']

items.title: Errors
items.text:
Error Exit code Raised when CheckFailedError 1 A check failed. NothingToReleaseError 1 No commit since the last release calls for one. ConfigError 2 Settings are invalid or live in two homes. EnvironmentProblemError 3 Git or gh cannot give a trustworthy answer.

All of them derive from GitVersionedError.

items.title: Logging
items.text:
gitversioned logs through Loguru. To get the same output as the command line:

from gitversioned.logging import configure_logging

configure_logging(1)  # -1 errors only, 0 warnings, 1 info, 2 debug

items.title: Command Line Guide
items.text:
gitversioned has three commands, one per job, and an optional setup step.

Command Job version Print the version, print the next one, or stamp it into the files. check Validate the repository setup, a title, a commit range or a tag. release Plan a release, open the release pull request, tag the merge. init Optional: add the archive file and wire up the build backend.

Every command takes the same shared options.

Option Meaning -C, --root DIR Run as if started in DIR. -p, --package N Act on one package from [packages]. --json Machine-readable output on stdout, errors included. -v, -vv More detail on stderr. -q, --quiet Errors only.

Results go to stdout and everything else goes to stderr, so VERSION=$(gitversioned version) is always safe.

items.title: Exit codes
items.text: Code Meaning 0 Success. 1 A check failed, or there is nothing to release. 2 Wrong usage or invalid configuration. 3 The environment cannot give a trustworthy answer (shallow clone in CI, no git, gh missing).

items.title: version
items.text:
gitversioned version [VERSION] [--next] [--bump LEVEL] [--pre KIND]
                     [--type TYPE] [--standard STD]
                     [--write] [--dry-run] [--explain]

items.title: Print the version of this checkout
items.text:
$ gitversioned version
1.4.1.dev20261125+60439dc
$ gitversioned version --standard semver
1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc
$ gitversioned version --type nightly
1.5.0.dev20261125

On a release tag the output is the tag's version. After the tag it is a development version: the next patch, the commit date and the short commit hash. A changed tracked file adds .dirty. The default spelling is PEP 440 when the project has a pyproject.toml with a [project] table, and SemVer otherwise.

items.title: Print the next release
items.text:
$ gitversioned version --next
1.5.0
$ gitversioned version --next --pre rc
1.5.0rc1
$ gitversioned version --next --bump major
2.0.0

--next reads the Conventional Commit subjects since the last release. It exits with code 1 when no commit since then calls for a release.

items.title: See why
items.text:
$ gitversioned version --explain
version   1.4.1.dev20261125+60439dc
type      dev
current   1.4.0  (tag v1.4.0, 60439dc, 2 commits since)
why       minor: 1 patch, 1 minor
  patch   fix(cli): exit code on empty input
  minor   feat(core): add streaming parser
note      base 1.4.0 from tag v1.4.0
config    .config/gitversioned.toml  (6 keys set, 8 defaults)

items.title: Stamp the files
items.text:
$ gitversioned version --write
1.4.1.dev20261125+60439dc
  CITATION.cff            1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc
  Dockerfile              1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc
  charts/demo/Chart.yaml  1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc
  crates/cli/Cargo.toml   1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc
  crates/core/Cargo.toml  1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc
  src/demo/version.py     1.4.1.dev20261125+60439dc
  Cargo.lock              1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc
  docs/install.md         1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc

Each file gets the spelling its ecosystem expects. --dry-run prints a unified diff and changes nothing. Stamping never makes the tree count as dirty: a file whose only change is its version is ignored when the version is resolved again.

Pass a VERSION to use that version instead of resolving one, for example gitversioned version 2.0.0 --write.

items.text:
$ gitversioned version --json
{
  "version": "1.4.1.dev20261125+60439dc",
  "pep440": "1.4.1.dev20261125+60439dc",
  "semver": "1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc",
  "type": "dev",
  "source": "tag",
  "tag": "v1.4.0",
  "distance": 2,
  "sha": "60439dc",
  "dirty": false,

items.title: check
items.text: gitversioned check [TITLE] [--commits RANGE] [--tag NAME] [--file PATH] [--warn]

items.title: The repository setup
items.text:
$ gitversioned check
ok    config        .config/gitversioned.toml
ok    git           full history, 1 release tags, latest v1.4.0
ok    targets       CITATION.cff, Dockerfile, charts/demo/Chart.yaml, ...
ok    scopes        core, cli, web, chart, docs, deps
warn  archive file  .git_archival.txt is not set up, so source tarballs lose the version. Run `gitversioned init`.
warn  github        gh is missing or not signed in: release --pr and pull request titles in the changelog are unavailable.

Problems that only warn on a laptop fail in CI (when the CI environment variable is set), with exit code 3. The usual one is a shallow clone: set fetch-depth: 0 on actions/checkout.

items.title: A pull request title or commit message
items.text:
$ gitversioned check "feat(core): add a thing"
ok
$ gitversioned check "added a thing"
fail  title  'added a thing' is not a Conventional Commit title. Expected type(scope): subject. Types: feat, fix, perf, ...
$ gitversioned check --file .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG
$ gitversioned check --commits origin/main..HEAD
ok    commits  2 commits

--file reads the first line of a file, which is what a commit-msg hook passes. --warn reports problems and still exits 0.

items.title: A tag name
items.text:
$ gitversioned check --tag v1.5.0
ok    tag  1.5.0, newer than v1.4.0

Use this in a workflow that runs when a tag is pushed, to reject tags that do not match the template or that are not newer than the last release.

items.title: release
items.text:
gitversioned release [VERSION] [--bump LEVEL] [--pre KIND] [--write] [--pr] [--tag]

A release has three stages. Without a flag the command only shows the plan.

items.title: Plan
items.text:
$ gitversioned release
release   1.5.0  (minor, from commits, from 1.4.0)
tag       v1.5.0
files     CHANGELOG.md, CITATION.cff, Dockerfile, charts/demo/Chart.yaml, crates/cli/Cargo.toml, crates/core/Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, docs/install.md

## 1.5.0 - 2026-11-25

### Added

- **core**: add streaming parser

### Fixed

- **cli**: exit code on empty input

Nothing changed. Run with --write, --pr or --tag.

items.title: --write: update the working tree
items.text: Writes the changelog section and stamps every committed target. Nothing is committed, so this is the stage to use when you make the release commit yourself.

items.title: --pr: open or update the release pull request
items.text:
Rebuilds the branch release/next from the current commit with one commit titled release: v1.5.0, pushes it, and opens a pull request labelled release, or updates the one already open. The pull request body is the changelog section. Run it on every push to the release branch and the pull request always shows what the next release will be. It refuses to run on any other branch, and exits with code 1 when HEAD is a merged release commit that is not tagged yet, so it never reopens a release that is waiting for release --tag. It needs the GitHub CLI gh, signed in (GH_TOKEN in CI).

Add the label release:rc to the pull request to make it a release candidate. Add release:major, release:minor or release:patch to a merged pull request to override the level its title would give.

items.title: --tag: tag the merged release
items.text: Run on the branch setting's branch (main by default) right after the release pull request merges. It reads the tag from the release commit's subject, checks it is newer than the last release, creates it and pushes it. Pass a VERSION to tag HEAD by hand.

items.title: Choosing the version
items.text:
The first of these that is set decides:

  1. The VERSION argument.
  2. --bump major|minor|patch.
  3. GITVERSIONED__BUMP in the environment (a level or a version).
  4. A release:major|minor|patch label on a merged pull request.
  5. The commits since the last release.

items.title: init
items.text:
$ gitversioned init
wrote  .git_archival.txt
edit   .gitattributes          + .git_archival.txt  export-subst

Adds the two things a repository needs for a version to survive a source tarball from GitHub, and adds [tool.hatch.version] source = "gitversioned" to a Hatchling project that does not have it yet. It only creates files or appends to them. Nothing else in gitversioned depends on it.

items.title: Git hook for commit messages
items.text:
# .git/hooks/commit-msg
gitversioned check --file "$1"

items.title: Build a container with the right version
items.text:
gitversioned version --write
docker build --build-arg VERSION="$(gitversioned version --standard semver)" .

items.title: One package in a monorepo
items.text:
gitversioned version -p web
gitversioned release -p web --pr

items.title: One version, two spellings
items.text:
gitversioned keeps one version per checkout and prints it the way each ecosystem expects.

Build PEP 440 (Python) SemVer (Rust, npm, Helm, OCI) Release 1.2.0 1.2.0 Pre-release 1.2.0rc1 1.2.0-rc.1 Development 1.2.1.dev20261125+abc1234 1.2.1-dev.20261125+abc1234 Nightly 1.3.0.dev20261125 1.3.0-nightly.20261125 Dirty tree 1.2.1.dev20261125+abc1234.dirty 1.2.1-dev.20261125+abc1234.dirty

A development version is the next patch after the last release, dated with the commit date so the same commit always gives the same version. A nightly has no hash, so it can be uploaded to a package index. The hash is the first seven characters of the commit, lengthened only in the rare case where those would be all digits with a leading zero, which Python packaging tools would renumber.

items.title: Where the version comes from
items.text:
The first source that answers wins:

  1. A pin. A VERSION argument, GITVERSIONED__VERSION, or version = "1.2.3" in the settings.
  2. Git tags. The highest release tag reachable from HEAD that matches the tag template, plus the number of commits since.
  3. The archive file. .git_archival.txt, filled in by git archive, for source tarballs downloaded from GitHub. Files written for setuptools-scm are read too.
  4. Package metadata. PKG-INFO in an unpacked sdist.
  5. The fallback. 0.1.0 unless configured, with a warning.

There are no version files to keep in sync and no version committed between releases. A tag is the only thing that makes a release.

items.title: Warn on a laptop, fail in CI
items.text: When the answer cannot be trusted (a shallow clone with no tag in reach, no git history at all) gitversioned warns and uses the fallback on a developer machine. In CI, detected by the CI environment variable, the same situation exits with code 3 so a wrong version is never published.

items.title: How the next version is chosen
items.text:
version --next and release read the Conventional Commit subjects since the last release.

Commit Level feat!: ... or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer major feat: ... minor fix, perf, refactor, docs, build, revert, deprecate patch chore, ci, test, release, merge commits none

Below 1.0.0 every level shifts down one: a breaking change is a minor bump and a feature is a patch bump. An explicit --bump is taken as written.

items.title: Stamping
items.text: version --write puts the version into every target with scoped text edits. Only the characters of the version change; comments, ordering, quoting and line endings are kept. Because a stamped manifest differs from git only in its version, gitversioned does not count it as a dirty tree, so builds that stamp first and resolve later agree.

items.title: The release flow
items.text:
commits on main ──► gitversioned release --pr ──► release pull request
                                                    │  review, edit, merge
                                                    ▼
                    gitversioned release --tag ──► tag v1.5.0 ──► publish jobs

The release pull request holds one commit: the changelog section and the stamped manifests. It is rebuilt on every push to the release branch, so it always shows what the next release would be. Merging it is the decision to release; tagging the merge is what makes the version.

items.title: The changelog
items.text: Sections follow Keep a Changelog (Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security) with entries grouped by scope. chore, ci, test and release commits are left out unless they are breaking. When gh is available, the pull request title replaces a squash commit's subject, and a ## Changelog block in a pull request body replaces the generated entry. A final release replaces the sections of its release candidates.

items.title: Configuration Guide
items.text: gitversioned works with no configuration. Everything below is optional, and the whole surface is twelve settings, a list of extra files and a table of packages.

items.title: Where settings live
items.text:
Settings live in exactly one of these places, searched in this order from the folder the command runs in up to the repository root:

Home Table .config/gitversioned.toml The whole file gitversioned.toml The whole file pyproject.toml [tool.gitversioned] Cargo.toml [workspace.metadata.gitversioned] or [package.metadata.gitversioned] package.json "gitversioned" setup.cfg [tool:gitversioned]

Two homes in the same folder is an error that names both, so a setting can never be silently shadowed. An unknown key is also an error, and it names the nearest valid key.

items.title: The settings
items.text:
Key Default What it does version "auto" A pinned version, or auto to resolve from git. fallback "0.1.0" The base version before the first tag exists. tag "v{version}" The tag template; also how release tags are recognised. annotated false Create annotated tags that carry the changelog section. branch "main" The branch releases are cut from and release pull requests target. dev "patch" The base of a development build: patch, minor, major or next. nightly "next" The base of a nightly build; next is the next release from commits. date "commit" The date in dev and nightly versions: commit (reproducible) or build. local true Add +<hash> to development builds. changelog "CHANGELOG.md" The changelog file, or false to turn it off. types The twelve types below The commit types check accepts. scopes [] (any scope) The allowed scopes, or the path of a TOML file whose table names are the scopes.

The default types are feat, fix, perf, refactor, docs, test, build, ci, chore, revert, deprecate and release.

items.title: Example: every setting
items.text:
# .config/gitversioned.toml
version = "auto"
fallback = "0.1.0"
tag = "v{version}"
annotated = false
branch = "main"
dev = "patch"
nightly = "next"
date = "commit"
local = true
changelog = "CHANGELOG.md"
types = ["feat", "fix", "perf", "refactor", "docs", "test", "build", "ci", "chore", "revert", "deprecate", "release"]
scopes = ["core", "cli", "docs"]

The same settings in the other homes:

# pyproject.toml
[tool.gitversioned]
tag = "v{version}"
scopes = ["core", "cli", "docs"]

# Cargo.toml
[workspace.metadata.gitversioned]
tag = "v{version}"
scopes = ["core", "cli", "docs"]

{
  "name": "my-package",
  "gitversioned": {
    "tag": "v{version}",
    "scopes": ["core", "cli", "docs"]
  }
}

# setup.cfg
[tool:gitversioned]
tag = v{version}
scopes = ["core", "cli", "docs"]

items.title: Targets: the files that get stamped
items.text:
Discovery finds these files on its own, among the files git tracks:

File What is stamped Spelling pyproject.toml project.version, when it is static PEP 440 <package>/version.py Generated, when the build uses gitversioned and the version is dynamic PEP 440 Cargo.toml package.version or workspace.package.version, and the versions of path dependencies on workspace crates SemVer Cargo.lock The entries of the workspace crates SemVer package.json version SemVer tauri.conf.json version SemVer Chart.yaml version and appVersion SemVer CITATION.cff (root) version, and date-released on a release SemVer Dockerfile (root) The org.opencontainers.image.version label, unless it is a $VARIABLE SemVer

Files under node_modules, target, dist, build, site, examples, tests, test, testdata, fixtures, vendor and third_party are left alone. Edits are scoped text edits: only the version value changes, so comments, key order, quoting and line endings survive.

List any other file with [[targets]]:

# A value in a TOML, JSON or YAML file, by dotted key
[[targets]]
path = "deploy/values.yaml"
key = "image.tag"

# Any text file, by a regular expression with a `version` group
[[targets]]
path = "docs/install.md"
pattern = 'my-tool@(?P<version>[0-9][^\s`]*)'

# A file discovery would skip, or one that should not be committed
[[targets]]
path = "examples/demo/package.json"
commit = false
Key Meaning path The file, relative to the project root. Required. key Dotted path of the value in a TOML, JSON or YAML file. pattern Regular expression with a version group. Not together with key. commit Whether the release pull request commits the file. Defaults to true for manifests and false for generated files.

items.title: Packages: more than one version in a repository
items.text:
[packages.core]
path = "crates/core"              # follows the repository version

[packages.web]
path = "packages/web"
tag = "web-v{version}"            # its own tags, version and release pull request
Key Meaning path The package folder, relative to the project root. Required. tag A tag template. Without it the package follows the repository version.

A package with its own tag is versioned from its own tags, counts only the commits that touch its folder, and is left out of the repository's own version and stamping. Use -p NAME on any command to act on it. The package names are added to the allowed scopes.

items.title: Environment overrides
items.text:
Any setting can be overridden with GITVERSIONED__<KEY>. Lists and booleans are written as JSON. An unknown GITVERSIONED__ variable is ignored with a warning, since the environment is shared with other tools and older releases.

GITVERSIONED__VERSION=1.2.3 python -m build       # pin the version for one build
GITVERSIONED__LOCAL=false gitversioned version    # no +hash, e.g. for TestPyPI
GITVERSIONED__TAG='release-{version}' gitversioned version
GITVERSIONED__SCOPES='["core","cli"]' gitversioned check "feat(core): x"
GITVERSIONED__BUMP=minor gitversioned release     # a level or an exact version

gitversioned version --explain lists how many keys were set and where the settings were read from.

items.title: What is not configurable
items.text:
These are fixed on purpose, so every repository behaves the same way.

  • Bump rules. A breaking change is major, feat is minor, every other releasable type is patch. chore, ci, test and release commits and merge commits do not release. Below 1.0.0 each level shifts down one.
  • Release names. The branch is release/next, the pull request title is release: <tag>, and the labels are release, release:rc and release:major|minor|patch.
  • Changelog format. Keep a Changelog sections, grouped by scope.
  • Version sources. Tags, the archive file, sdist metadata, or a pin.

items.title: GitHub Workflows Guide
items.text:
Three small jobs cover the whole release flow. Every job that reads a version needs full history:

- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0

Without it, gitversioned exits with code 3 in CI instead of publishing a wrong version.

items.title: Check pull request titles
items.text:
name: pr-title
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, edited, synchronize, reopened]
jobs:
  title:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: pipx run gitversioned check "$TITLE"
        env:
          TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}

With squash merges the pull request title becomes the commit subject, so this one check keeps the history releasable.

items.title: Keep the release pull request up to date
items.text:
name: release-pr
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
jobs:
  release-pr:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - run: pipx run gitversioned release --pr || [ $? -eq 1 ]
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

Exit code 1 means there is nothing to release yet, which is not a failure here. Pull requests opened with the default GITHUB_TOKEN do not start other workflows; use a GitHub App token or a personal access token if your checks must run on the release pull request.

items.title: Tag the merged release and publish
items.text:
name: release
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: write
jobs:
  tag:
    if: startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'release')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - run: pipx run gitversioned release --tag
      - run: pipx run build
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1

release --tag reads the tag from the merged release commit, refuses a tag that is not newer than the last release, and pushes it.

items.title: Development and nightly builds
items.text:
- run: |
    pipx run gitversioned version --write --type nightly
    echo "VERSION=$(pipx run gitversioned version --type nightly)" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

--type dev is the default away from a tag. --type nightly has no commit hash and can be uploaded to a package index.

items.title: Reject bad tags
items.text:
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - run: pipx run gitversioned check --tag "$GITHUB_REF_NAME"

items.title: Hatchling Guide
items.text: gitversioned plugs into Hatchling as a version source and a build hook. The version comes from git at build time and nothing is committed.

items.title: Setup
items.text:
# pyproject.toml
[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling", "gitversioned>=0.4"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "my-package"
dynamic = ["version"]

[tool.hatch.version]
source = "gitversioned"

[tool.hatch.build.hooks.gitversioned]
Piece What it does gitversioned in requires Makes the plugin available to the isolated build. dynamic = ["version"] Tells the build the version is not in the file. [tool.hatch.version] source Resolves the version from git. [tool.hatch.build.hooks.gitversioned] Writes <package>/version.py and adds it to the wheel and sdist.

gitversioned init adds the [tool.hatch.version] table for you.

items.title: Read the version at runtime
items.text:
Add the generated file to .gitignore, then import from it:

src/my_package/version.py

# src/my_package/__init__.py
from my_package.version import __version__

The generated module holds __version__, __version_semver__, __version_tuple__, __tag__, __distance__, __commit__ and __commit_date__. It has no build timestamp, so two builds of one commit are identical.

items.title: Build
items.text:
$ git tag v1.2.3
$ python -m build
Successfully built my_package-1.2.3.tar.gz and my_package-1.2.3-py3-none-any.whl

After the tag the same command builds 1.2.4.dev20261125+abc1234. A wheel built from the unpacked sdist keeps the sdist's version, because the version is read from PKG-INFO when there is no git history.

items.title: Publishing development builds
items.text:
Package indexes reject versions with a local part (+abc1234). Build a nightly, which has none, or turn the hash off:

gitversioned version --type nightly --write && python -m build
GITVERSIONED__LOCAL=false python -m build

items.title: Settings
items.text: Settings go under [tool.gitversioned], never under the Hatch tables. See the Configuration Guide. A runnable project is in examples/hatchling.

items.title: Maturin Guide
items.text: Maturin takes the version of a Rust extension from Cargo.toml. gitversioned wraps Maturin's build backend: it stamps the resolved version into Cargo.toml for the length of the build, hands over to Maturin, then restores the file.

items.title: Setup
items.text:
# pyproject.toml
[build-system]
requires = ["maturin>=1.0,<2.0", "gitversioned>=0.4"]
build-backend = "gitversioned.plugins.maturin"

[project]
name = "my-extension"
dynamic = ["version"]

[tool.maturin]
python-source = "python"
module-name = "my_extension._native"

# Cargo.toml
[package]
name = "my-extension"
version = "0.0.0"        # a placeholder; never edited by hand

Everything under [tool.maturin] is passed through untouched.

items.title: Build
items.text:
$ git tag v0.3.0
$ python -m build --wheel
$ git status --short

The wheel is my_extension-0.3.0-...whl and the working tree is clean afterwards. Release candidates are spelled for each side: a tag v0.3.0-rc.1 gives the wheel version 0.3.0rc1 and the crate version 0.3.0-rc.1.

items.title: Cargo on its own
items.text:
For cargo build, cargo publish or maturin develop outside a PEP 517 build, stamp the manifests first:

gitversioned version --write
cargo build --release

In a workspace this also updates the version of every path dependency on a workspace crate (the operator, such as = or ^, is kept) and the matching Cargo.lock entries, so cargo build --locked keeps working. The stamped files do not make the tree count as dirty.

A runnable project is in examples/maturin.

items.title: Migrating from 0.3
items.text: Version 0.4 is a rewrite with no compatibility layer. The tool now covers Python, Rust and npm manifests, checks Conventional Commits and drives releases, and its surface is much smaller.

items.title: Commands
items.text: 0.3 0.4 gitversioned calculate gitversioned version gitversioned calculate --version-type nightly gitversioned version --type nightly gitversioned write gitversioned version --write gitversioned format gitversioned version --write --dry-run gitversioned overrides gitversioned version --write (targets are discovered) gitversioned init-archive gitversioned init No equivalent gitversioned check, gitversioned release

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Old keys are rejected with an error that names the nearest new key.

0.3 0.4 output, output_strategies Removed. version.py is generated in one fixed shape. overrides [[targets]] with key or pattern; most files are discovered. version_type --type on the command line. version_standard --standard; each file gets its own spelling. regex_tag and the other regex_* keys tag = "v{version}". format_main, format_dev, format_pre, format_post Fixed shapes; choose the base with dev and nightly. auto_increment dev and nightly. source_type, version_source_* Removed. Sources are tried in a fixed order. dirty_ignore Removed. Stamped files never count as dirty.

Environment overrides are spelled GITVERSIONED__KEY, with two underscores.

items.title: Build backends
items.text: Backend Change Hatchling Keep source = "gitversioned". Add [tool.hatch.build.hooks.gitversioned] for version.py. Setuptools Now opt-in: list gitversioned in build-system.requires. Maturin Set build-backend = "gitversioned.plugins.maturin".

items.title: Version shapes
items.text: Development versions changed from a commit count to the commit date: 1.2.1.dev4+gabc1234 is now 1.2.1.dev20261125+abc1234. Nightly versions have no local part. Tags are read the same way, so existing tags keep working.

items.title: Python API
items.text: Settings, the strategy classes and the template helpers are gone. Use load_config, resolve, stamp and plan_release; see the API Guide.

items.title: Setuptools Guide
items.text: The setuptools integration is opt-in, so installing gitversioned next to an unrelated setuptools project never changes that project's version.

items.title: Setup
items.text:
# pyproject.toml
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=64", "gitversioned>=0.4"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "my-package"
dynamic = ["version"]

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

Listing gitversioned in build-system.requires is the opt-in. A project that still uses setup.py can opt in with a keyword instead:

# setup.py
from setuptools import setup

setup(gitversioned=True)

items.title: What the build does
items.text:
The build resolves the version from git, sets it as the distribution's version and writes <package>/version.py so the installed package can report it. Add that file to .gitignore:

src/my_package/version.py

# src/my_package/__init__.py
from my_package.version import __version__

$ git tag v2.1.0
$ python -m build --wheel
Successfully built my_package-2.1.0-py3-none-any.whl

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Settings can live in [tool.gitversioned] in pyproject.toml or in [tool:gitversioned] in setup.cfg:

# setup.cfg
[tool:gitversioned]
fallback = 0.1.0
scopes = ["core", "docs"]

See the Configuration Guide. A runnable project is in examples/setuptools.

items.title: Coming from setuptools-scm
items.text:
• Tags are read the same way, so existing v1.2.3 tags keep working.
  • An existing .git_archival.txt is read as it is.
  • write_to / version_file is replaced by the generated version.py.
  • Remove setuptools-scm from build-system.requires and delete [tool.setuptools_scm].

items.title: Python API Usage
items.text:
gitversioned can be used from your own Python code:

from gitversioned import get_version, load_config, resolve

print(get_version())

resolved = resolve(load_config())
print(resolved.version.semver(), resolved.type, resolved.source)

See the API Guide for more.

items.title: CLI
items.text: This page documents the CLI for gitversioned.

items.title: gitversioned
items.text:
Versions from git tags, stamped into every manifest, checked and released.

Usage:

$ gitversioned [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Options:

  • --version: Print the version of gitversioned itself.
  • --help: Show this message and exit.

Commands:

  • version: Print the version; --next for the upcoming...
  • check: Validate the repo setup, a pull request...
  • release: Plan a release; --pr to open the release...
  • init: Optional: add the archive file and wire up...

items.title: gitversioned version
items.text:
Print the version; --next for the upcoming release; --write to stamp files.

Usage:

$ gitversioned version [OPTIONS] [[VERSION]]

Arguments:

  • [VERSION] <str>: Use this version instead of resolving one.

Options:

  • --next: The version the next release would get.
  • --bump LEVEL: With --next: force major, minor or patch.
  • --pre KIND: With --next: rc, beta or alpha.
  • --type TYPE: Force dev, nightly or release.
  • --standard STD: Print as pep440 or semver.
  • --write: Stamp the version into every target.
  • --dry-run: With --write: show the diff, change nothing.
  • --explain: Show how the answer was reached.
  • -C, --root DIR: Run as if started in DIR.
  • -p, --package NAME: Act on one package from [packages].
  • --json: Machine-readable output on stdout.
  • -v, --verbose: More detail on stderr (-vv for debug). [default: 0]
  • -q, --quiet: Errors only.
  • --help: Show this message and exit.

items.title: gitversioned check
items.text:
Validate the repo setup, a pull request title, commits or a tag.

Usage:

$ gitversioned check [OPTIONS] [[TITLE]]

Arguments:

  • [TITLE] <str>: A pull request title or commit subject to validate.

Options:

  • --commits RANGE: Validate every commit subject in a git range.
  • --tag NAME: Validate a tag name.
  • --file PATH: Read the message from a file (commit-msg hook).
  • --warn: Report problems but exit 0.
  • -C, --root DIR: Run as if started in DIR.
  • -p, --package NAME: Act on one package from [packages].
  • --json: Machine-readable output on stdout.
  • -v, --verbose: More detail on stderr (-vv for debug). [default: 0]
  • -q, --quiet: Errors only.
  • --help: Show this message and exit.

items.title: gitversioned release
items.text:
Plan a release; --pr to open the release pull request; --tag to tag it.

Usage:

$ gitversioned release [OPTIONS] [[VERSION]]

Arguments:

  • [VERSION] <str>: Release exactly this version.

Options:

  • --bump LEVEL: Override the level chosen from commits and labels.
  • --pre KIND: Make it a pre-release: rc, beta or alpha.
  • --write: Update the changelog and committed targets in the working tree.
  • --pr: Commit the release to the release branch and open or update the PR.
  • --tag: Tag the release commit and push the tag.
  • -C, --root DIR: Run as if started in DIR.
  • -p, --package NAME: Act on one package from [packages].
  • --json: Machine-readable output on stdout.
  • -v, --verbose: More detail on stderr (-vv for debug). [default: 0]
  • -q, --quiet: Errors only.
  • --help: Show this message and exit.

items.title: gitversioned init
items.text:
Optional: add the archive file and wire up the build backend.

Usage:

$ gitversioned init [OPTIONS]

Options:

  • -C, --root DIR: Run as if started in DIR.
  • --json: Machine-readable output on stdout.
  • -v, --verbose: More detail on stderr (-vv for debug). [default: 0]
  • -q, --quiet: Errors only.
  • --help: Show this message and exit.

items.title: gitversioned
items.text:
Versions from git tags for Python, Rust and npm projects in one repository.

gitversioned resolves the version of a checkout from its release tags, stamps it into every manifest with scoped text edits, validates Conventional Commit titles and drives a reviewed release: changelog, release pull request and tag.

Example: :: from gitversioned import get_version, load_config, resolve

print(get_version())
resolved = resolve(load_config())
print(resolved.version.semver(), resolved.type)

class Config(BaseModel):
    """
    Every setting gitversioned has.

    :param version: A pinned version, or ``auto`` to resolve from git.
    :param fallback: Base version when no tag exists yet.
    :param tag: Tag template; also how release tags are recognised.
    :param annotated: Create annotated tags carrying the changelog section.
    :param branch: Branch releases are cut from.
    :param dev: Base of a development build.
    :param nightly: Base of a nightly build.
    :param date: Date used in development and nightly versions.
    :param local: Add the commit hash to development builds.
    :param changelog: Changelog file, or ``False`` to turn it off.
    :param types: Allowed commit types.
    :param scopes: Allowed scopes, or a TOML file whose table names are the scopes.
    :param targets: Extra files to stamp.
    :param packages: Packages with their own folder and optional tag.
    :param root: Project root the paths are relative to.
    :param home: Where the settings were read from, for messages.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    version: str = "auto"
    fallback: str = "0.1.0"
    tag: str = "v{version}"
    annotated: bool = False
    branch: str = "main"
    dev: BumpBase = "patch"
    nightly: BumpBase = "next"
    date: Literal["commit", "build"] = "commit"
    local: bool = True
    changelog: str | Literal[False] = "CHANGELOG.md"
    types: list[str] = Field(default_factory=lambda: list(DEFAULT_TYPES))
    scopes: list[str] | str = Field(default_factory=list)
    targets: list[TargetConfig] = Field(default_factory=list)
    packages: dict[str, PackageConfig] = Field(default_factory=dict)

    root: Path = Field(default_factory=Path.cwd, exclude=True)
    home: str = Field(default="defaults", exclude=True)
    keys_set: tuple[str, ...] = Field(default=(), exclude=True)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _tag_template(self) -> Config:
        if "{version}" not in self.tag:
            raise ValueError("`tag` must contain {version}")
        return self

    def allowed_scopes(self) -> list[str]:
        """
        Resolve the allowed scopes, reading the scopes file when one is named.

        Package names are always allowed once any scope is restricted.

        :return: Scope names; an empty list allows any scope.
        :raises ConfigError: If the scopes file is missing or not valid TOML.
        """
        if isinstance(self.scopes, list):
            scopes = list(self.scopes)
        else:
            path = self.root / self.scopes
            try:
                data = tomllib.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            except (OSError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError) as error:
                raise ConfigError(f"cannot read scopes file {path}: {error}") from error
            scopes = [key for key, value in data.items() if isinstance(value, dict)]
        if scopes:
            scopes += [name for name in self.packages if name not in scopes]
        return scopes

    @classmethod
    def key_names(cls) -> list[str]:
        """
        :return: The names of the settings a home may hold.
        """
        return [name for name, field in cls.model_fields.items() if not field.exclude]

    """

    sha: str | None = None
    date: datetime | None = None

    @property
    def short_sha(self) -> str | None:
        """
        Shorten the commit hash for the local part of a version.

        Python packaging tools read an all-digit local part as a number and drop
        its leading zeros, so a hash that would be shortened to such a value is
        lengthened until it holds a letter.

        :return: At least the first seven characters of the commit hash.
        """
        if not self.sha:
            return None
        length = _SHORT_SHA
        while (
            length < len(self.sha)
            and self.sha[:length].isdigit()
            and self.sha.startswith("0")
        ):
            length += 1
        return self.sha[:length]

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Version:
    """
    A version with the parts PEP 440 and SemVer have in common.

    :param major: Major release number.
    :param minor: Minor release number.
    :param patch: Patch release number.
    :param pre: Pre-release kind and number, such as ``("rc", 1)``.
    :param dev: Development number, normally a ``YYYYMMDD`` date.
    :param local: Local build label, normally the short commit hash.
    :param nightly: Whether the development number marks a nightly build, which
        changes only the SemVer spelling.
    """

    major: int
    minor: int
    patch: int
    pre: tuple[str, int] | None = None
    dev: int | None = None
    local: str | None = None
    nightly: bool = False

    @classmethod
    def parse(cls, text: str) -> Version:
        """
        Parse a version or tag spelling in PEP 440 or SemVer form.

        :param text: Text such as ``1.2.3``, ``v1.3.0-rc.1``, ``1.3.0rc1`` or
            ``1.2.1.dev20261125+abc1234``.
        :return: The parsed version.
        :raises ConfigError: If the text is not a recognised version.
        """
        found = cls.try_parse(text)
        if found is None:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"not a version: {text!r}. Expected X.Y.Z with an optional "
                "pre-release such as -rc.1 or rc1."
            )
        return found

    @classmethod
    def try_parse(cls, text: str) -> Version | None:
        """
        Parse a version spelling, returning ``None`` when it does not match.

        :param text: Candidate version text.
        :return: The parsed version, or ``None``.
        """
        match = _VERSION_RE.match(text.strip())
        if match is None:
            return None
        pre: tuple[str, int] | None = None
        if match["pre"]:
            pre = (_PRE_ALIASES[match["pre"].lower()], int(match["pre_num"] or 0))
        dev = None
        if match["dev_kind"]:
            dev = int(match["dev"] or 0)
        return cls(
            major=int(match["major"]),
            minor=int(match["minor"]),
            patch=int(match["patch"]),
            pre=pre,
            dev=dev,
            local=match["local"],
            nightly=(match["dev_kind"] or "").lower() == "nightly",
        )

    @property
    def release(self) -> Version:
        """
        :return: The plain ``X.Y.Z`` release this version belongs to.
        """
        return Version(self.major, self.minor, self.patch)

    @property
    def is_final(self) -> bool:
        """
        :return: True for a plain ``X.Y.Z`` release.
        """
        return self.pre is None and self.dev is None

    def bump(self, level: str) -> Version:
        """
        Return the next plain release at the given level.

        :param level: Which part to raise.
        :return: A plain ``X.Y.Z`` version.
        """
        if level == "major":
            return Version(self.major + 1, 0, 0)
        if level == "minor":
            return Version(self.major, self.minor + 1, 0)
        return Version(self.major, self.minor, self.patch + 1)

    def with_parts(
        self,
        *,
        pre: tuple[str, int] | None = None,
        dev: int | None = None,
        local: str | None = None,
        nightly: bool = False,
    ) -> Version:
        """
        Return a copy with the variable parts replaced.

        :param pre: Pre-release kind and number.
        :param dev: Development number.
        :param local: Local build label.
        :param nightly: Whether the development number marks a nightly.
        :return: The new version.
        """
        return replace(self, pre=pre, dev=dev, local=local, nightly=nightly)

    def pep440(self) -> str:
        """
        :return: The PEP 440 spelling, such as ``1.3.0rc1.dev20261125+abc1234``.
        """
        text = f"{self.major}.{self.minor}.{self.patch}"
        if self.pre is not None:
            text += f"{_PRE_PEP440[self.pre[0]]}{self.pre[1]}"
        if self.dev is not None:
            text += f".dev{self.dev}"
        if self.local:
            text += "+" + re.sub(r"[^0-9A-Za-z.]", ".", self.local)
        return text

    def semver(self) -> str:
        """
        :return: The SemVer spelling, such as ``1.3.0-rc.1`` or
            ``1.2.1-dev.20261125+abc1234``.
        """
        text = f"{self.major}.{self.minor}.{self.patch}"
        parts: list[str] = []
        if self.pre is not None:
            parts += [self.pre[0], str(self.pre[1])]
        if self.dev is not None:
            parts += ["nightly" if self.nightly else "dev", str(self.dev)]
        if parts:
            text += "-" + ".".join(parts)
        if self.local:
            text += "+" + re.sub(r"[^0-9A-Za-z.-]", ".", self.local)
        return text

    def render(self, standard: str) -> str:
        """
        Print the version in the given standard.

        :param standard: ``pep440`` or ``semver``.
        :return: The version text.
        """
        return self.pep440() if standard == "pep440" else self.semver()

    def sort_key(self) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int, int, int]:
        """
        Return a key ordering versions the way both standards agree on.

        A development build sorts before its release, a pre-release sorts before
        the final, and a final sorts last for the same ``X.Y.Z``.

        :return: A tuple usable with ``sorted`` and ``max``.
        """
        if self.pre is not None:
            pre_rank, pre_num = _PRE_ORDER[self.pre[0]], self.pre[1]
        elif self.dev is not None:
            pre_rank, pre_num = -1, 0
        else:
            pre_rank, pre_num = 3, 0
        dev_rank, dev_num = (1, 0) if self.dev is None else (0, self.dev)
        return (
            self.major,
            self.minor,
            self.patch,
            pre_rank,
            pre_num,
            dev_rank,
            dev_num,
        )

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.pep440()

@classmethod
def try_parse(cls, text: str) -> Version | None:
    """
    Parse a version spelling, returning ``None`` when it does not match.

    :param text: Candidate version text.
    :return: The parsed version, or ``None``.
    """
    match = _VERSION_RE.match(text.strip())
    if match is None:
        return None
    pre: tuple[str, int] | None = None
    if match["pre"]:
        pre = (_PRE_ALIASES[match["pre"].lower()], int(match["pre_num"] or 0))
    dev = None
    if match["dev_kind"]:
        dev = int(match["dev"] or 0)
    return cls(
        major=int(match["major"]),
        minor=int(match["minor"]),
        patch=int(match["patch"]),
        pre=pre,
        dev=dev,
        local=match["local"],
        nightly=(match["dev_kind"] or "").lower() == "nightly",
    )

def load_config(
    start: Path | None = None, *, env: dict[str, str] | None = None
) -> Config:
    """
    Load the configuration for a project.

    :param start: Folder the command was started in; defaults to the current one.
    :param env: Environment to read overrides from; defaults to ``os.environ``.
    :return: The validated configuration.
    :raises ConfigError: For two homes, an unknown key or an invalid value.
    """
    environment = os.environ if env is None else env
    root = find_root(start or Path.cwd())
    homes = find_homes(root)
    if len(homes) > 1:
        names = " and ".join(label for label, _ in homes)
        raise ConfigError(
            f"settings found in two homes: {names}. Keep them in one file."
        )
    label, table = homes[0] if homes else ("defaults", {})
    if not isinstance(table, dict):
        raise ConfigError(f"{label} must be a table")
    data: dict[str, Any] = dict(table)
    valid = Config.key_names()
    for name in data:
        if name not in valid:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"unknown key `{name}` in {label}.{_suggest(name, valid)} "
                f"Valid keys: {', '.join(valid)}."
            )
    keys_set = sorted(data)
    for name, value in environment.items():
        if not name.startswith(ENV_PREFIX):
            continue
        key = name[len(ENV_PREFIX) :].lower()
        if key == "bump":
            continue
        if key not in valid:
            # The environment is shared with other tools and older gitversioned
            # releases, so a stale variable warns instead of stopping a build.
            logger.warning(
                "ignoring unknown environment override {}.{}",
                name,
                _suggest(key, valid),
            )
            continue
        data[key] = _coerce(value) if key not in ("version", "fallback") else value
        keys_set.append(f"{key} (env)")
    try:
        config = Config(**data)
    except ValidationError as error:
        problems = "; ".join(
            f"{'.'.join(str(part) for part in item['loc']) or 'config'}: {item['msg']}"
            for item in error.errors()
        )
        raise ConfigError(f"invalid config in {label}: {problems}") from error
    config.root = root
    config.home = label
    config.keys_set = tuple(keys_set)
    return config

def plan_release(  # noqa: PLR0913
    config: Config,
    *,
    version: str | None = None,
    bump: str | None = None,
    pre: str | None = None,
    package: str | None = None,
    use_github: bool = True,
) -> ReleasePlan:
    """
    Compute what a release would do, changing nothing.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param version: Version to release exactly.
    :param bump: Level that replaces the one chosen from commits.
    :param pre: Make the release a pre-release of this kind.
    :param package: Package to release instead of the repository.
    :param use_github: Read pull request titles, bodies and labels through ``gh``
        when it is available.
    :return: The plan.
    :raises NothingToReleaseError: If nothing releasable happened since the last
        release and no override is given.
    :raises CheckFailedError: If the chosen version is not newer than the last
        release.
    """
    repo = _require_repo(config)
    _require_own_tag(config, package)
    template, scope = package_context(config, package)
    resolved = resolve(config, tag_template=template, path_scope=scope)

    merged = repo.tags_merged()
    tags = release_tags(template, list(merged))
    finals = {name: found for name, found in tags.items() if found.is_final}
    last_final = (
        max(finals, key=lambda name: finals[name].sort_key()) if finals else None
    )
    scope_path = (config.root / scope) if scope else None
    excluded = [] if scope_path else own_tag_folders(config)
    since_final = repo.commits(
        merged[last_final] if last_final else None, path=scope_path, exclude=excluded
    )
    since_tag = repo.commits(
        merged[resolved.tag] if resolved.tag else None,
        path=scope_path,
        exclude=excluded,
    )
    requests = _pull_requests(config, since_final, use_github)
    explicit, chosen, source = _overrides(
        version, bump, _label_bump(since_tag, requests)
    )
    target = next_version(
        resolved.base,
        resolved.known,
        resolved.plan,
        fallback=Version.parse(config.fallback),
        explicit=explicit,
        bump=chosen,
        pre=pre,
    )
    if resolved.base is not None and target.sort_key() <= resolved.base.sort_key():
        raise CheckFailedError(
            f"{target.pep440()} is not newer than {resolved.tag} "
            f"({resolved.base.pep440()})."
        )
    entries = entries_from_commits(since_final, requests)
    day = datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    name = tag_name(template, target)
    prefix = f"release({package})" if package else "release"
    return ReleasePlan(
        version=target,
        previous=resolved.base,
        tag=name,
        level=_level_text(resolved, explicit, chosen, source),
        section=render_section(
            target, entries, day=day, repo_url=github.repo_url(repo)
        ),
        files=_release_files(config, package),
        entries=entries,
        bump=resolved.plan,
        package=package,
        title=f"{prefix}: {name}",
        branch=f"{RELEASE_BRANCH}-{package}" if package else RELEASE_BRANCH,
    )

:param config: The loaded configuration. :param resolved: The version to write. :param dry_run: Compute the changes and diffs without touching any file. :param package: Limit the work to one package from [packages]. :param committed_only: Skip targets the release pull request does not commit. :param generated_only: Write only the generated version.py files, as a build backend does. :return: One change per target, in discovery order.

def stamp(
    config: Config,
    resolved: Resolved,
    *,
    dry_run: bool = False,
    package: str | None = None,
    committed_only: bool = False,
    generated_only: bool = False,
) -> list[Change]:
    """
    Write the resolved version into every target.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param resolved: The version to write.
    :param dry_run: Compute the changes and diffs without touching any file.
    :param package: Limit the work to one package from ``[packages]``.
    :param committed_only: Skip targets the release pull request does not commit.
    :param generated_only: Write only the generated ``version.py`` files, as a
        build backend does.
    :return: One change per target, in discovery order.
    """
    changes: list[Change] = []
    for target in discover(config, package=package):
        if committed_only and not target.commit:
            continue
        if generated_only and not target.generated:
            continue
        relative = _relative(target.path, config.root)
        rendered = resolved.version.render(target.standard)
        old_text = _read_exact(target.path) if target.path.is_file() else ""
        if target.generated:
            old = _generated_version(old_text)
            new_text = render_version_module(resolved)
        else:
            old = target.current(old_text)
            new_text = target.apply(old_text, _values(target, resolved))
        diff = "".join(
            difflib.unified_diff(
                old_text.splitlines(keepends=True),
                new_text.splitlines(keepends=True),
                f"a/{relative}",
                f"b/{relative}",
            )
        )
        changed = new_text != old_text
        if changed and not dry_run:
            target.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with target.path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
                handle.write(new_text)
        changes.append(
            Change(
                relative, old, rendered, diff, target.commit, changed and not dry_run
            )
        )
    return changes

A pull request title replaces its squash commit subject, and a ## Changelog block in the pull request body replaces both.

def entries_from_commits(
    commits: list[Commit], pull_requests: dict[int, PullRequest] | None = None
) -> list[Entry]:
    """
    Turn commits into changelog entries.

    A pull request title replaces its squash commit subject, and a
    ``## Changelog`` block in the pull request body replaces both.

    :param commits: Commits since the previous release, newest first.
    :param pull_requests: Pull requests by number, when GitHub was reachable.
    :return: Entries in commit order, oldest first, with hidden types left out.
    """
    known = pull_requests or {}
    entries: list[Entry] = []
    for commit in reversed(commits):
        parsed = parse_subject(commit.subject, commit.body, commit.sha)
        number = parsed.pr if parsed else None
        if number is None:
            suffix = re.search(r"\(#(\d+)\)\s*$", commit.subject)
            number = int(suffix.group(1)) if suffix else None
        request = known.get(number) if number is not None else None
        if request is not None:
            retitled = parse_subject(request.title, request.body)
            if retitled is not None:
                parsed = retitled
        if parsed is None:
            continue
        if parsed.type in NO_RELEASE_TYPES and not parsed.breaking:
            continue
        kind = _TYPE_KIND.get(parsed.type, "Changed")
        if request is not None:
            block = _from_block(request.body, kind, parsed.scope, number)
            if block:
                entries.extend(block)
                continue
        entries.append(
            Entry(kind, parsed.scope, parsed.subject, number, parsed.breaking)
        )
    return entries

A section for the same version is replaced, and pre-release sections of the same release are removed, so a release pull request can be rebuilt freely.

def insert_section(text: str, version: Version, section: str) -> str:
    """
    Put a release section into a changelog, touching nothing else.

    A section for the same version is replaced, and pre-release sections of the
    same release are removed, so a release pull request can be rebuilt freely.

    :param text: Current changelog content; empty for a new file.
    :param version: Version of the section.
    :param section: Rendered section.
    :return: The new changelog content.
    """
    if not text.strip():
        text = _HEADER
    for name, start, end in reversed(_sections(text)):
        found = Version.try_parse(name)
        if found is None:
            continue
        if found == version or (
            found.pre is not None and found.release == version.release
        ):
            text = text[:start] + text[end:]
    position = len(text)
    for name, start, _end in _sections(text):
        if Version.try_parse(name) is not None:
            position = start
            break
    before = text[:position]
    if before and not before.endswith("\n\n"):
        before = before.rstrip("\n") + "\n\n"
    after = text[position:]
    block = section.rstrip("\n") + "\n"
    return before + block + ("\n" + after if after else "")

def read_section(path: Path, version: Version) -> str | None:
    """
    Read the section of one version back out of a changelog file.

    :param path: Changelog file.
    :param version: Version to find.
    :return: The section text, or ``None``.
    """
    if not path.is_file():
        return None
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for name, start, end in _sections(text):
        if Version.try_parse(name) == version:
            return text[start:end].strip() + "\n"
    return None

def render_section(
    version: Version,
    entries: list[Entry],
    *,
    day: str,
    repo_url: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """
    Render one release section.

    :param version: Version being released.
    :param entries: Entries to list.
    :param day: Release date as ``YYYY-MM-DD``.
    :param repo_url: Repository web address, used to link pull requests.
    :return: Markdown ending in a newline.
    """
    lines = [f"## {version.semver()} - {day}", ""]
    for kind in KINDS:
        chosen = [entry for entry in entries if entry.kind == kind]
        if not chosen:
            continue
        chosen.sort(
            key=lambda entry: (
                not entry.breaking,
                entry.scope is None,
                entry.scope or "",
            )
        )
        lines += [f"### {kind}", ""]
        for entry in chosen:
            text = entry.text
            if entry.breaking:
                text = f"**Breaking:** {text}"
            if entry.scope:
                text = f"**{entry.scope}**: {text}"
            if entry.pr is not None:
                link = (
                    f"[#{entry.pr}]({repo_url}/pull/{entry.pr})"
                    if repo_url
                    else f"#{entry.pr}"
                )
                text += f" ({link})"
            lines.append(f"- {text}")
        lines.append("")
    if not entries:
        lines += ["No notable changes.", ""]
    return "\n".join(lines)

def check_commits(config: Config, revision_range: str) -> list[Finding]:
    """
    Validate every commit subject in a git range.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param revision_range: A range such as ``origin/main..HEAD``.
    :return: One finding per invalid commit, or a single ``ok`` finding.
    """
    repo = git.Repo.open(config.root)
    if repo is None:
        return [Finding("fail", "commits", "not a git repository.", exit_code=3)]
    since, _, ref = revision_range.partition("..")
    if repo.git("rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", since, check=False) is None:
        return [Finding("fail", "commits", f"unknown revision {since!r}.", exit_code=2)]
    commits = repo.commits(since, ref or "HEAD")
    problems: list[Finding] = []
    for commit in commits:
        if commit.subject.startswith(("Merge ", 'Revert "')):
            continue
        found = check_title(config, commit.subject, area=commit.sha[:7])
        problems += [item for item in found if item.status == "fail"]
    return problems or [Finding("ok", "commits", f"{len(commits)} commits")]

def check_tag(
    config: Config, name: str, *, template: str | None = None
) -> list[Finding]:
    """
    Validate a tag name and that it is newer than the last release.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param name: Tag name to validate.
    :param template: Tag template to use instead of the configured one.
    :return: A single finding.
    """
    pattern = template or config.tag
    version = match_tag(pattern, name)
    if version is None:
        return [
            Finding(
                "fail",
                "tag",
                f"{name!r} is not a release tag. Expected "
                f"{pattern.replace('{version}', 'X.Y.Z')} with an optional "
                "pre-release such as -rc.1.",
            )
        ]
    repo = git.Repo.open(config.root)
    existing: dict[str, Version] = {}
    if repo is not None:
        existing = release_tags(
            pattern, [tag for tag in repo.all_tags() if tag != name]
        )
    if existing:
        latest = max(existing, key=lambda tag: existing[tag].sort_key())
        if version.sort_key() <= existing[latest].sort_key():
            return [
                Finding(
                    "fail",
                    "tag",
                    f"{version.pep440()} is not newer than {latest}.",
                )
            ]
        return [Finding("ok", "tag", f"{version.pep440()}, newer than {latest}")]
    return [Finding("ok", "tag", f"{version.pep440()}, first release")]

def check_title(config: Config, title: str, area: str = "title") -> list[Finding]:
    """
    Validate a pull request title or commit subject.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param title: The title to validate.
    :param area: Label for the report line.
    :return: A single ``ok`` finding, or one finding per problem.
    """
    parsed = parse_subject(title)
    if parsed is None:
        return [
            Finding(
                "fail",
                area,
                f"{title!r} is not a Conventional Commit title. Expected "
                f"type(scope): subject. Types: {', '.join(config.types)}.",
            )
        ]
    problems: list[Finding] = []
    if parsed.type not in config.types:
        problems.append(
            Finding(
                "fail",
                area,
                f"unknown type {parsed.type!r}. Types: {', '.join(config.types)}.",
            )
        )
    scopes = config.allowed_scopes()
    if parsed.scope and scopes:
        unknown = [
            scope.strip()
            for scope in parsed.scope.split(",")
            if scope.strip() not in scopes
        ]
        if unknown:
            problems.append(
                Finding(
                    "fail",
                    area,
                    f"unknown scope {unknown[0]!r}. Scopes: {', '.join(scopes)}.",
                )
            )
    return problems or [Finding("ok", area, title)]

            config,
            version=version,
            bump=bump,
            pre=pre,
            package=package,
        )

        bump=bump,
        pre=pre,

    _choice(pre, _PRE, "--pre")
    _choice(build_type, _TYPES, "--type")
    _choice(standard, _STANDARDS, "--standard")

        raise ConfigError("--bump and --pre need --next.")
    if dry_run and not write:
        raise ConfigError("--dry-run needs --write.")
    config = load_config(root)
    template, scope = package_context(config, package)
    resolved = resolve(
        config,
        pin=version,
        build_type=cast("BuildType | None", build_type),
        tag_template=template,
        path_scope=scope,
    )
    spelling = standard or _default_standard(config)
    upcoming: Version | None = None
    if next_release:
        upcoming = _next(config, resolved, bump, pre)
        resolved = dataclasses.replace(resolved, version=upcoming, type="release")
    changes = stamp(config, resolved, dry_run=dry_run, package=package) if write else []
    if json_output:

        if upcoming is None:
            try:
                document["next"] = _next(config, resolved, None, None).render(spelling)
            except NothingToReleaseError:
                document["next"] = None
        else:
            document["next"] = upcoming.render(spelling)
        _emit(document)
        return
    if explain:
        for line in _explain(config, resolved, upcoming, spelling):
            typer.echo(line)
    else:
        typer.echo(resolved.version.render(spelling))
    if write:
        _print_changes(changes, dry_run)

Conventional Commit parsing and the rules that choose the next version.

The rules are fixed: a breaking change raises major, feat raises minor, any other change raises patch, and chore, ci, test and release commits alone do not justify a release. Below 1.0 every level shifts down by one.

def level_of(parsed: ParsedCommit | None, subject: str = "") -> Level | None:
    """
    Decide the level one commit asks for.

    :param parsed: The parsed commit, or ``None`` for an unconventional subject.
    :param subject: The raw subject, used to skip merge commits.
    :return: ``major``, ``minor``, ``patch`` or ``None`` for no release.
    """
    if parsed is None:
        return None if _MERGE_RE.match(subject) else "patch"
    if parsed.breaking:
        return "major"
    if parsed.type == "feat":
        return "minor"
    if parsed.type in NO_RELEASE_TYPES:
        return None
    return "patch"

Overrides win in this order: an explicit version, an explicit level, then the commits. A pre-release numbers itself after the existing tags of its kind.

:param current: The latest released version, or None before the first tag. :param known: Every version already tagged, used to number pre-releases. :param plan: What the commits ask for. :param fallback: First version of a repository with no tags. :param explicit: A version to release exactly, or a level name. :param bump: A level that replaces the one chosen from commits. :param pre: Make the result a pre-release of this kind. :return: The version to release. :raises NothingToReleaseError: If no override is given and no commit is releasable. :raises ConfigError: If an override is neither a level nor a version.

Source code in src/gitversioned/commits.py 
def next_version(
    current: Version | None,
    known: list[Version],
    plan: BumpPlan,
    *,
    fallback: Version,
    explicit: str | None = None,
    bump: str | None = None,
    pre: str | None = None,
) -> Version:
    """
    Choose the next release version.

    Overrides win in this order: an explicit version, an explicit level, then the
    commits. A pre-release numbers itself after the existing tags of its kind.

    :param current: The latest released version, or ``None`` before the first tag.
    :param known: Every version already tagged, used to number pre-releases.
    :param plan: What the commits ask for.
    :param fallback: First version of a repository with no tags.
    :param explicit: A version to release exactly, or a level name.
    :param bump: A level that replaces the one chosen from commits.
    :param pre: Make the result a pre-release of this kind.
    :return: The version to release.
    :raises NothingToReleaseError: If no override is given and no commit is
        releasable.
    :raises ConfigError: If an override is neither a level nor a version.
    """
    if explicit and explicit not in _LEVEL_RANK:
        target = Version.parse(explicit)
        if pre is None:
            return target
        target = target.release
    else:
        level_name = explicit or bump
        if level_name is not None and level_name not in _LEVEL_RANK:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"not a bump level: {level_name!r}. Use major, minor or patch."
            )
        if current is None:
            target = fallback.release
        elif current.pre is not None and level_name is None:
            target = current.release
        elif level_name is not None:
            target = current.release.bump(level_name)
        elif plan.level is None:
            raise NothingToReleaseError("Nothing to release: no releasable commits.")
        else:
            target = current.bump(_shift(plan.level, current))
    if pre is None:
        return target
    numbers = [
        version.pre[1]
        for version in known
        if version.pre is not None
        and version.dev is None
        and version.pre[0] == pre
        and version.release == target
    ]
    return target.with_parts(pre=(pre, max(numbers, default=0) + 1))

def parse_subject(
    subject: str, body: str = "", sha: str | None = None
) -> ParsedCommit | None:
    """
    Parse a commit subject or pull request title.

    :param subject: First line of the message.
    :param body: Rest of the message, searched for a breaking-change footer.
    :param sha: Commit hash to carry along.
    :return: The parsed parts, or ``None`` when the subject is not conventional.
    """
    match = _SUBJECT_RE.match(subject.strip())
    if match is None:
        return None
    text = match["subject"]
    pr: int | None = None
    pr_match = _PR_RE.search(text)
    if pr_match:
        pr = int(pr_match["pr"])
        text = text[: pr_match.start()]
    return ParsedCommit(
        type=match["type"].lower(),
        scope=match["scope"].strip() if match["scope"] else None,
        breaking=bool(match["breaking"]) or bool(_BREAKING_RE.search(body)),
        subject=text.strip(),
        pr=pr,
        sha=sha,
    )

def plan_bump(commits: list[Commit]) -> BumpPlan:
    """
    Find the highest level a list of commits asks for.

    :param commits: Commits since the last release.
    :return: The level and the per-commit reasons.
    """
    reasons: list[tuple[Level | None, Commit]] = []
    best: Level | None = None
    for commit in commits:
        level = level_of(parse_subject(commit.subject, commit.body), commit.subject)
        reasons.append((level, commit))
        if level is not None and (
            best is None or _LEVEL_RANK[level] > _LEVEL_RANK[best]
        ):
            best = level
    return BumpPlan(level=best, reasons=tuple(reasons))
