class Config(BaseModel):
    """
    Every setting gitversioned has.

    :param version: A pinned version, or ``auto`` to resolve from git.
    :param fallback: Base version when no tag exists yet.
    :param tag: Tag template; also how release tags are recognised.
    :param annotated: Create annotated tags carrying the changelog section.
    :param branch: Branch releases are cut from.
    :param dev: Base of a development build.
    :param nightly: Base of a nightly build.
    :param date: Date used in development and nightly versions.
    :param local: Add the commit hash to development builds.
    :param changelog: Changelog file, or ``False`` to turn it off.
    :param types: Allowed commit types.
    :param scopes: Allowed scopes, or a TOML file whose table names are the scopes.
    :param targets: Extra files to stamp.
    :param packages: Packages with their own folder and optional tag.
    :param root: Project root the paths are relative to.
    :param home: Where the settings were read from, for messages.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    version: str = "auto"
    fallback: str = "0.1.0"
    tag: str = "v{version}"
    annotated: bool = False
    branch: str = "main"
    dev: BumpBase = "patch"
    nightly: BumpBase = "next"
    date: Literal["commit", "build"] = "commit"
    local: bool = True
    changelog: str | Literal[False] = "CHANGELOG.md"
    types: list[str] = Field(default_factory=lambda: list(DEFAULT_TYPES))
    scopes: list[str] | str = Field(default_factory=list)
    targets: list[TargetConfig] = Field(default_factory=list)
    packages: dict[str, PackageConfig] = Field(default_factory=dict)

    root: Path = Field(default_factory=Path.cwd, exclude=True)
    home: str = Field(default="defaults", exclude=True)
    keys_set: tuple[str, ...] = Field(default=(), exclude=True)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _tag_template(self) -> Config:
        if "{version}" not in self.tag:
            raise ValueError("`tag` must contain {version}")
        return self

    def allowed_scopes(self) -> list[str]:
        """
        Resolve the allowed scopes, reading the scopes file when one is named.

        Package names are always allowed once any scope is restricted.

        :return: Scope names; an empty list allows any scope.
        :raises ConfigError: If the scopes file is missing or not valid TOML.
        """
        if isinstance(self.scopes, list):
            scopes = list(self.scopes)
        else:
            path = self.root / self.scopes
            try:
                data = tomllib.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            except (OSError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError) as error:
                raise ConfigError(f"cannot read scopes file {path}: {error}") from error
            scopes = [key for key, value in data.items() if isinstance(value, dict)]
        if scopes:
            scopes += [name for name in self.packages if name not in scopes]
        return scopes

    @classmethod
    def key_names(cls) -> list[str]:
        """
        :return: The names of the settings a home may hold.
        """
        return [name for name, field in cls.model_fields.items() if not field.exclude]

def allowed_scopes(self) -> list[str]:
    """
    Resolve the allowed scopes, reading the scopes file when one is named.

    Package names are always allowed once any scope is restricted.

    :return: Scope names; an empty list allows any scope.
    :raises ConfigError: If the scopes file is missing or not valid TOML.
    """
    if isinstance(self.scopes, list):
        scopes = list(self.scopes)
    else:
        path = self.root / self.scopes
        try:
            data = tomllib.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError) as error:
            raise ConfigError(f"cannot read scopes file {path}: {error}") from error
        scopes = [key for key, value in data.items() if isinstance(value, dict)]
    if scopes:
        scopes += [name for name in self.packages if name not in scopes]
    return scopes

def find_root(start: Path) -> Path:
    """
    Find the project root for a starting folder.

    The root is the nearest parent holding a config home or an unpacked source
    distribution (``PKG-INFO``), searching no higher than the repository root;
    failing that the repository root, then the start.

    :param start: Folder the command was started in.
    :return: The project root.
    """
    start = start.resolve()
    repo = git.Repo.open(start)
    top = repo.top if repo is not None else None
    current = start
    while True:
        if find_homes(current) or (current / "PKG-INFO").is_file():
            return current
        if current in (top, current.parent):
            break
        current = current.parent
    return top if top is not None and _inside(start, top) else start

def load_config(
    start: Path | None = None, *, env: dict[str, str] | None = None
) -> Config:
    """
    Load the configuration for a project.

    :param start: Folder the command was started in; defaults to the current one.
    :param env: Environment to read overrides from; defaults to ``os.environ``.
    :return: The validated configuration.
    :raises ConfigError: For two homes, an unknown key or an invalid value.
    """
    environment = os.environ if env is None else env
    root = find_root(start or Path.cwd())
    homes = find_homes(root)
    if len(homes) > 1:
        names = " and ".join(label for label, _ in homes)
        raise ConfigError(
            f"settings found in two homes: {names}. Keep them in one file."
        )
    label, table = homes[0] if homes else ("defaults", {})
    if not isinstance(table, dict):
        raise ConfigError(f"{label} must be a table")
    data: dict[str, Any] = dict(table)
    valid = Config.key_names()
    for name in data:
        if name not in valid:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"unknown key `{name}` in {label}.{_suggest(name, valid)} "
                f"Valid keys: {', '.join(valid)}."
            )
    keys_set = sorted(data)
    for name, value in environment.items():
        if not name.startswith(ENV_PREFIX):
            continue
        key = name[len(ENV_PREFIX) :].lower()
        if key == "bump":
            continue
        if key not in valid:
            # The environment is shared with other tools and older gitversioned
            # releases, so a stale variable warns instead of stopping a build.
            logger.warning(
                "ignoring unknown environment override {}.{}",
                name,
                _suggest(key, valid),
            )
            continue
        data[key] = _coerce(value) if key not in ("version", "fallback") else value
        keys_set.append(f"{key} (env)")
    try:
        config = Config(**data)
    except ValidationError as error:
        problems = "; ".join(
            f"{'.'.join(str(part) for part in item['loc']) or 'config'}: {item['msg']}"
            for item in error.errors()
        )
        raise ConfigError(f"invalid config in {label}: {problems}") from error
    config.root = root
    config.home = label
    config.keys_set = tuple(keys_set)
    return config

def toml_span(text: str, path: list[str]) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    """
    Find a string value in a TOML document by dotted path.

    The path is split into a table and a key at every possible point, so
    ``["tool", "poetry", "version"]`` finds ``version`` under ``[tool.poetry]``
    and also ``poetry.version`` under ``[tool]``.

    :param text: TOML source.
    :param path: Keys from the root to the value.
    :return: Start and end of the value between its quotes, or ``None``.
    """
    tables = toml_table_spans(text)
    for split in range(len(path) - 1, -1, -1):
        table = ".".join(path[:split])
        pattern = _toml_key_pattern(".".join(path[split:]))
        for name, start, end in tables:
            if name != table:
                continue
            offset = start
            for line in text[start:end].splitlines(keepends=True):
                match = pattern.match(line)
                if match:
                    return offset + match.start("value"), offset + match.end("value")
                offset += len(line)
    return None

def toml_table_spans(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]:
    """
    List the tables of a TOML document with the span of each body.

    :param text: TOML source.
    :return: Table name, body start and body end; the root table is named ``""``.
    """
    tables: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = []
    name = ""
    start = 0
    offset = 0
    for line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
        match = _TOML_HEADER.match(line.rstrip("\r\n"))
        if match and "=" not in line.split("#")[0].split("]")[-1]:
            tables.append((name, start, offset))
            name = _normal_table(match["name"])
            start = offset + len(line)
        offset += len(line)
    tables.append((name, start, len(text)))
    return tables

def yaml_span(text: str, path: list[str]) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    """
    Find a scalar value in a block-style YAML document by key path.

    :param text: YAML source.
    :param path: Mapping keys from the root to the value.
    :return: Start and end of the scalar, inside its quotes when quoted, or
        ``None``.
    """
    depth = 0
    parent_indent = -1
    child_indent: int | None = None
    offset = 0
    for line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
        bare = line.rstrip("\r\n")
        line_offset = offset
        offset += len(line)
        if not bare.strip() or bare.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        match = _YAML_LINE.match(bare)
        indent = len(bare) - len(bare.lstrip())
        if indent <= parent_indent:
            if depth == 0:
                continue
            return None
        if match is None:
            continue
        if child_indent is None:
            child_indent = indent
        if indent != child_indent:
            continue
        key = match["key"].strip().strip("\"'")
        if key != path[depth]:
            continue
        if depth == len(path) - 1:
            rest = match["rest"] or ""
            return (
                _yaml_scalar(rest, line_offset + match.start("rest")) if rest else None
            )
        depth += 1
        parent_indent = indent
        child_indent = None
    return None

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Repo:
    """
    A git repository seen from a project folder inside it.

    :param top: Repository root.
    :param cwd: Project folder the commands run from.
    """

    top: Path
    cwd: Path

    @classmethod
    def open(cls, cwd: Path) -> Repo | None:
        """
        Open the repository containing a folder.

        :param cwd: Any folder inside the work tree.
        :return: The repository, or ``None`` when git is missing or the folder is
            not in a work tree.
        """
        if not cwd.is_dir():
            return None
        top = run(["rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], cwd, check=False)
        if not top:
            return None
        return cls(top=Path(top).resolve(), cwd=cwd.resolve())

    def git(self, *args: str, check: bool = True) -> str | None:
        """
        Run a git command from the repository root.

        :param args: Arguments after ``git``.
        :param check: When False, failure returns ``None``.
        :return: The command output.
        """
        return run(list(args), self.top, check=check)

    def head(self) -> str | None:
        """
        :return: The full hash of ``HEAD``, or ``None`` in a repository with no
            commits.
        """
        return self.git("rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", "HEAD", check=False) or None

    def head_date(self) -> datetime | None:
        """
        :return: The committer date of ``HEAD`` in UTC.
        """
        stamp = self.git("log", "-1", "--format=%ct", check=False)
        if not stamp:
            return None
        return datetime.fromtimestamp(int(stamp), tz=timezone.utc)

    def branch(self) -> str | None:
        """
        :return: The current branch name, or ``None`` on a detached ``HEAD``.
        """
        return self.git("symbolic-ref", "--short", "-q", "HEAD", check=False) or None

    def is_shallow(self) -> bool:
        """
        :return: True when history was cut by a shallow clone.
        """
        return self.git("rev-parse", "--is-shallow-repository", check=False) == "true"

    def tags_merged(self, ref: str = "HEAD") -> dict[str, str]:
        """
        List the tags reachable from a ref with the commit each one points at.

        Annotated tags are peeled, so the hash is always a commit.

        :param ref: Ref the tags must be reachable from.
        :return: Tag name to commit hash.
        """
        out = self.git(
            "for-each-ref",
            "--merged",
            ref,
            "--format=%(refname:short)%1f%(objectname)%1f%(*objectname)",
            "refs/tags",
            check=False,
        )
        tags: dict[str, str] = {}
        for line in (out or "").splitlines():
            name, obj, peeled = (line.split(_FIELD_SEP) + ["", ""])[:3]
            tags[name] = peeled or obj
        return tags

    def all_tags(self) -> list[str]:
        """
        :return: Every tag name in the repository.
        """
        out = self.git("tag", "--list", check=False)
        return out.splitlines() if out else []

    def distance(self, since: str | None, ref: str = "HEAD") -> int:
        """
        Count the commits on a ref after a starting point.

        :param since: Commit or tag to count from; ``None`` counts all history.
        :param ref: Ref to count to.
        :return: Number of commits.
        """
        spec = f"{since}..{ref}" if since else ref
        out = self.git("rev-list", "--count", spec, check=False)
        return int(out) if out and out.isdigit() else 0

    def commits(
        self,
        since: str | None,
        ref: str = "HEAD",
        path: Path | None = None,
        exclude: list[Path] | None = None,
    ) -> list[Commit]:
        """
        List the commits on a ref after a starting point, newest first.

        :param since: Commit or tag to start after; ``None`` lists all history.
        :param ref: Ref to list to.
        :param path: Only commits touching this folder, for a package.
        :param exclude: Folders whose commits do not count, for packages that
            carry their own tags.
        :return: The commits.
        """
        spec = f"{since}..{ref}" if since else ref
        args = ["log", f"--format=%H{_FIELD_SEP}%s{_FIELD_SEP}%b{_RECORD_SEP}", spec]
        if path is not None:
            args += ["--", str(path)]
        elif exclude:
            args += [
                "--",
                ".",
                *[f":(exclude){self.relative(item)}" for item in exclude],
            ]
        out = self.git(*args, check=False) or ""
        commits: list[Commit] = []
        for record in out.split(_RECORD_SEP):
            if not record.strip():
                continue
            sha, subject, body = (record.strip("\n").split(_FIELD_SEP) + ["", ""])[:3]
            commits.append(Commit(sha=sha, subject=subject, body=body.strip()))
        return commits

    def dirty_paths(self) -> list[str]:
        """
        List tracked files with uncommitted changes, relative to the repository root.

        Untracked files do not count, matching ``git describe --dirty``.

        :return: Paths with staged or unstaged changes.
        """
        out = self.git(
            "status", "--porcelain=v1", "--untracked-files=no", "-z", check=False
        )
        paths: list[str] = []
        entries = (out or "").split("\0")
        index = 0
        while index < len(entries):
            entry = entries[index]
            index += 1
            if len(entry) <= _STATUS_PREFIX:
                continue
            paths.append(entry[_STATUS_PREFIX:])
            if entry[0] in "RC":
                index += 1
        return paths

    def show(self, path: str, ref: str = "HEAD") -> str | None:
        """
        Read a file as committed.

        :param path: Path relative to the repository root.
        :param ref: Commit to read from.
        :return: The file text, or ``None`` when it does not exist there.
        """
        return self.git("show", f"{ref}:{path}", check=False)

    def tracked_files(self) -> list[str]:
        """
        :return: Tracked and untracked-but-not-ignored files, relative to the root.
        """
        out = self.git(
            "ls-files", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard", check=False
        )
        return out.splitlines() if out else []

    def tracks(self, folder: Path) -> bool:
        """
        Tell whether git tracks anything in a folder.

        :param folder: Folder inside the work tree.
        :return: True when at least one tracked file lies in the folder.
        """
        out = self.git("ls-files", "--", self.relative(folder) or ".", check=False)
        return bool(out)

    def relative(self, path: Path) -> str:
        """
        Express a path relative to the repository root with forward slashes.

        :param path: Absolute path inside the work tree.
        :return: The relative path.
        """
        return path.resolve().relative_to(self.top).as_posix()

    spec = f"{since}..{ref}" if since else ref
    args = ["log", f"--format=%H{_FIELD_SEP}%s{_FIELD_SEP}%b{_RECORD_SEP}", spec]
    if path is not None:
        args += ["--", str(path)]
    elif exclude:
        args += [
            "--",
            ".",
            *[f":(exclude){self.relative(item)}" for item in exclude],
        ]
    out = self.git(*args, check=False) or ""
    commits: list[Commit] = []
    for record in out.split(_RECORD_SEP):
        if not record.strip():
            continue
        sha, subject, body = (record.strip("\n").split(_FIELD_SEP) + ["", ""])[:3]
        commits.append(Commit(sha=sha, subject=subject, body=body.strip()))
    return commits

def dirty_paths(self) -> list[str]:

    Untracked files do not count, matching ``git describe --dirty``.

    :return: Paths with staged or unstaged changes.

        if entry[0] in "RC":

    return paths

Read a git archive export file in either supported layout.

Both the setuptools-scm layout (node, node-date, describe-name, ref-names) and the gitversioned layout (commit_sha, commit_date, ref_names) are accepted. A file that was never expanded is ignored.

:param root: Folder holding .git_archival.txt. :return: The archive details, or None when absent or unexpanded.

def read_archive(root: Path) -> ArchiveInfo | None:
    """
    Read a ``git archive`` export file in either supported layout.

    Both the setuptools-scm layout (``node``, ``node-date``, ``describe-name``,
    ``ref-names``) and the gitversioned layout (``commit_sha``, ``commit_date``,
    ``ref_names``) are accepted. A file that was never expanded is ignored.

    :param root: Folder holding ``.git_archival.txt``.
    :return: The archive details, or ``None`` when absent or unexpanded.
    """
    path = root / ARCHIVE_FILE
    if not path.is_file():
        return None
    fields: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
        key, sep, value = line.partition(":")
        if sep:
            fields[key.strip().lower().replace("_", "-")] = value.strip()
    values = {
        key: value
        for key, value in fields.items()
        if value and "$Format" not in value and not value.startswith("%")
    }
    if not values:
        return None
    sha = values.get("node") or values.get("commit-sha")
    tags, distance = _archive_tags(values)
    date: datetime | None = None
    raw_date = values.get("node-date") or values.get("commit-date")
    if raw_date:
        try:
            date = datetime.fromisoformat(raw_date).astimezone(timezone.utc)
        except ValueError:
            date = None
    if not sha and not tags:
        return None
    return ArchiveInfo(sha=sha, tags=tuple(tags), distance=distance, date=date)

def repo_url(repo: git.Repo) -> str | None:
    """
    Work out the web address of the repository from its ``origin`` remote.

    :param repo: The repository.
    :return: An ``https://github.com/owner/name`` address, or ``None``.
    """
    remote = repo.git("remote", "get-url", "origin", check=False)
    if not remote:
        return None
    match = re.match(
        r"^(?:https?://|git@|ssh://git@)(?P<host>[^/:]+)[/:](?P<path>.+?)(?:\.git)?/?$",
        remote.strip(),
    )
    if match is None or "github" not in match["host"]:
        return None
    return f"https://{match['host']}/{match['path']}"

:param major: Major release number. :param minor: Minor release number. :param patch: Patch release number. :param pre: Pre-release kind and number, such as ("rc", 1). :param dev: Development number, normally a YYYYMMDD date. :param local: Local build label, normally the short commit hash. :param nightly: Whether the development number marks a nightly build, which changes only the SemVer spelling.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Version:
    """
    A version with the parts PEP 440 and SemVer have in common.

    :param major: Major release number.
    :param minor: Minor release number.
    :param patch: Patch release number.
    :param pre: Pre-release kind and number, such as ``("rc", 1)``.
    :param dev: Development number, normally a ``YYYYMMDD`` date.
    :param local: Local build label, normally the short commit hash.
    :param nightly: Whether the development number marks a nightly build, which
        changes only the SemVer spelling.
    """

    major: int
    minor: int
    patch: int
    pre: tuple[str, int] | None = None
    dev: int | None = None
    local: str | None = None
    nightly: bool = False

    @classmethod
    def parse(cls, text: str) -> Version:
        """
        Parse a version or tag spelling in PEP 440 or SemVer form.

        :param text: Text such as ``1.2.3``, ``v1.3.0-rc.1``, ``1.3.0rc1`` or
            ``1.2.1.dev20261125+abc1234``.
        :return: The parsed version.
        :raises ConfigError: If the text is not a recognised version.
        """
        found = cls.try_parse(text)
        if found is None:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"not a version: {text!r}. Expected X.Y.Z with an optional "
                "pre-release such as -rc.1 or rc1."
            )
        return found

    @classmethod
    def try_parse(cls, text: str) -> Version | None:
        """
        Parse a version spelling, returning ``None`` when it does not match.

        :param text: Candidate version text.
        :return: The parsed version, or ``None``.
        """
        match = _VERSION_RE.match(text.strip())
        if match is None:
            return None
        pre: tuple[str, int] | None = None
        if match["pre"]:
            pre = (_PRE_ALIASES[match["pre"].lower()], int(match["pre_num"] or 0))
        dev = None
        if match["dev_kind"]:
            dev = int(match["dev"] or 0)
        return cls(
            major=int(match["major"]),
            minor=int(match["minor"]),
            patch=int(match["patch"]),
            pre=pre,
            dev=dev,
            local=match["local"],
            nightly=(match["dev_kind"] or "").lower() == "nightly",
        )

    @property
    def release(self) -> Version:
        """
        :return: The plain ``X.Y.Z`` release this version belongs to.
        """
        return Version(self.major, self.minor, self.patch)

    @property
    def is_final(self) -> bool:
        """
        :return: True for a plain ``X.Y.Z`` release.
        """
        return self.pre is None and self.dev is None

    def bump(self, level: str) -> Version:
        """
        Return the next plain release at the given level.

        :param level: Which part to raise.
        :return: A plain ``X.Y.Z`` version.
        """
        if level == "major":
            return Version(self.major + 1, 0, 0)
        if level == "minor":
            return Version(self.major, self.minor + 1, 0)
        return Version(self.major, self.minor, self.patch + 1)

    def with_parts(
        self,
        *,
        pre: tuple[str, int] | None = None,
        dev: int | None = None,
        local: str | None = None,
        nightly: bool = False,
    ) -> Version:
        """
        Return a copy with the variable parts replaced.

        :param pre: Pre-release kind and number.
        :param dev: Development number.
        :param local: Local build label.
        :param nightly: Whether the development number marks a nightly.
        :return: The new version.
        """
        return replace(self, pre=pre, dev=dev, local=local, nightly=nightly)

    def pep440(self) -> str:
        """
        :return: The PEP 440 spelling, such as ``1.3.0rc1.dev20261125+abc1234``.
        """
        text = f"{self.major}.{self.minor}.{self.patch}"
        if self.pre is not None:
            text += f"{_PRE_PEP440[self.pre[0]]}{self.pre[1]}"
        if self.dev is not None:
            text += f".dev{self.dev}"
        if self.local:
            text += "+" + re.sub(r"[^0-9A-Za-z.]", ".", self.local)
        return text

    def semver(self) -> str:
        """
        :return: The SemVer spelling, such as ``1.3.0-rc.1`` or
            ``1.2.1-dev.20261125+abc1234``.
        """
        text = f"{self.major}.{self.minor}.{self.patch}"
        parts: list[str] = []
        if self.pre is not None:
            parts += [self.pre[0], str(self.pre[1])]
        if self.dev is not None:
            parts += ["nightly" if self.nightly else "dev", str(self.dev)]
        if parts:
            text += "-" + ".".join(parts)
        if self.local:
            text += "+" + re.sub(r"[^0-9A-Za-z.-]", ".", self.local)
        return text

    def render(self, standard: str) -> str:
        """
        Print the version in the given standard.

        :param standard: ``pep440`` or ``semver``.
        :return: The version text.
        """
        return self.pep440() if standard == "pep440" else self.semver()

    def sort_key(self) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int, int, int]:
        """
        Return a key ordering versions the way both standards agree on.

        A development build sorts before its release, a pre-release sorts before
        the final, and a final sorts last for the same ``X.Y.Z``.

        :return: A tuple usable with ``sorted`` and ``max``.
        """
        if self.pre is not None:
            pre_rank, pre_num = _PRE_ORDER[self.pre[0]], self.pre[1]
        elif self.dev is not None:
            pre_rank, pre_num = -1, 0
        else:
            pre_rank, pre_num = 3, 0
        dev_rank, dev_num = (1, 0) if self.dev is None else (0, self.dev)
        return (
            self.major,
            self.minor,
            self.patch,
            pre_rank,
            pre_num,
            dev_rank,
            dev_num,
        )

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.pep440()

@classmethod
def try_parse(cls, text: str) -> Version | None:
    """
    Parse a version spelling, returning ``None`` when it does not match.

    :param text: Candidate version text.
    :return: The parsed version, or ``None``.
    """
    match = _VERSION_RE.match(text.strip())
    if match is None:
        return None
    pre: tuple[str, int] | None = None
    if match["pre"]:
        pre = (_PRE_ALIASES[match["pre"].lower()], int(match["pre_num"] or 0))
    dev = None
    if match["dev_kind"]:
        dev = int(match["dev"] or 0)
    return cls(
        major=int(match["major"]),
        minor=int(match["minor"]),
        patch=int(match["patch"]),
        pre=pre,
        dev=dev,
        local=match["local"],
        nightly=(match["dev_kind"] or "").lower() == "nightly",
    )

The release flow: plan, write, pull request and tag.

A plan is computed first and changes nothing. The three stages build on it: writing edits the changelog and the committed targets, the pull request stage commits those edits to the release branch and opens or updates the pull request, and the tag stage tags the merged release commit.

plan = plan_release(load_config(), use_github=False)

def open_release_pr(
    config: Config,
    *,
    version: str | None = None,
    bump: str | None = None,
    pre: str | None = None,
    package: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[ReleasePlan, github.PullRequest, bool]:
    """
    Open the release pull request, or update the one already open.

    The release branch is rebuilt from the current commit every time, so the pull
    request always holds exactly one commit on top of the release branch's base.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param version: Version to release exactly.
    :param bump: Level that replaces the one chosen from commits.
    :param pre: Make the release a pre-release of this kind.
    :param package: Package to release instead of the repository.
    :return: The plan, the pull request and whether it was newly opened.
    :raises CheckFailedError: If the working tree has uncommitted changes or
        the command runs on a branch other than the release branch.
    :raises NothingToReleaseError: If ``HEAD`` is a merged release commit whose
        tag does not exist yet, so the release is still waiting for its tag.
    """
    repo = _require_repo(config)
    if not github.available(config.root):
        raise EnvironmentProblemError(
            "release --pr needs the GitHub CLI `gh`, signed in (set GH_TOKEN in CI)."
        )
    if repo.dirty_paths():
        raise CheckFailedError(
            "the working tree has uncommitted changes; commit or stash them first."
        )
    current = repo.branch()
    if current is not None and current != config.branch:
        raise CheckFailedError(
            f"release --pr runs on {config.branch!r}, not {current!r}: the release "
            "would carry this branch's unmerged commits."
        )
    _require_own_tag(config, package)
    pending = _released_tag(repo, package)
    if pending is not None and pending not in repo.all_tags():
        raise NothingToReleaseError(
            f"HEAD is the merged release commit for {pending}, which is not tagged "
            "yet. Run release --tag first."
        )
    branch = f"{RELEASE_BRANCH}-{package}" if package else RELEASE_BRANCH
    existing = github.find_open_pull_request(config.root, branch)
    if pre is None and existing is not None and RC_LABEL in existing.labels:
        pre = "rc"
    plan = plan_release(config, version=version, bump=bump, pre=pre, package=package)

    start = current or repo.head() or "HEAD"
    repo.git("checkout", "-q", "-B", plan.branch)
    try:
        changed = write_release(config, plan)
        root_in_repo = config.root.resolve().relative_to(repo.top).as_posix()
        paths = [
            path if root_in_repo == "." else f"{root_in_repo}/{path}"
            for path in changed
        ]
        if paths:
            repo.git("add", "--", *paths)
        repo.git(*_identity(repo), "commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", plan.title)
        repo.git("push", "-q", "--force", "origin", plan.branch)
    except BaseException:
        # Leave no release edits behind on the branch the command started from.
        repo.git("reset", "-q", "--hard", check=False)
        raise
    finally:
        repo.git("checkout", "-q", start, check=False)

    body = (
        f"{plan.section}\n---\n"
        f"Merging this pull request releases `{plan.tag}`. "
        f"Add the `{RC_LABEL}` label to make it a release candidate.\n"
    )
    if existing is None:
        request = github.create_pull_request(
            config.root,
            head=plan.branch,
            base=config.branch,
            title=plan.title,
            body=body,
            label=RELEASE_LABEL,
        )
        return plan, request, True
    github.update_pull_request(
        config.root, existing.number, title=plan.title, body=body
    )
    return plan, existing, False

def package_context(config: Config, package: str | None) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
    """
    Work out the tag template and commit scope for the repository or a package.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param package: Package name from ``[packages]``, or ``None``.
    :return: The tag template and the folder whose commits count.
    :raises ConfigError: If the package is unknown.
    """
    if package is None:

    if package not in config.packages:
        raise ConfigError(
            f"unknown package {package!r}. Packages: "
            f"{', '.join(config.packages) or 'none configured'}."

    item = config.packages[package]
    if item.tag is None:
        return config.tag, None
    return item.tag, item.path

def plan_release(  # noqa: PLR0913
    config: Config,
    *,
    version: str | None = None,
    bump: str | None = None,
    pre: str | None = None,
    package: str | None = None,
    use_github: bool = True,
) -> ReleasePlan:
    """
    Compute what a release would do, changing nothing.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param version: Version to release exactly.
    :param bump: Level that replaces the one chosen from commits.
    :param pre: Make the release a pre-release of this kind.
    :param package: Package to release instead of the repository.
    :param use_github: Read pull request titles, bodies and labels through ``gh``
        when it is available.
    :return: The plan.
    :raises NothingToReleaseError: If nothing releasable happened since the last
        release and no override is given.
    :raises CheckFailedError: If the chosen version is not newer than the last
        release.
    """
    repo = _require_repo(config)
    _require_own_tag(config, package)
    template, scope = package_context(config, package)
    resolved = resolve(config, tag_template=template, path_scope=scope)

    merged = repo.tags_merged()
    tags = release_tags(template, list(merged))
    finals = {name: found for name, found in tags.items() if found.is_final}
    last_final = (
        max(finals, key=lambda name: finals[name].sort_key()) if finals else None
    )
    scope_path = (config.root / scope) if scope else None
    excluded = [] if scope_path else own_tag_folders(config)
    since_final = repo.commits(
        merged[last_final] if last_final else None, path=scope_path, exclude=excluded
    )
    since_tag = repo.commits(
        merged[resolved.tag] if resolved.tag else None,
        path=scope_path,
        exclude=excluded,
    )
    requests = _pull_requests(config, since_final, use_github)
    explicit, chosen, source = _overrides(
        version, bump, _label_bump(since_tag, requests)
    )
    target = next_version(
        resolved.base,
        resolved.known,
        resolved.plan,
        fallback=Version.parse(config.fallback),
        explicit=explicit,
        bump=chosen,
        pre=pre,
    )
    if resolved.base is not None and target.sort_key() <= resolved.base.sort_key():
        raise CheckFailedError(
            f"{target.pep440()} is not newer than {resolved.tag} "
            f"({resolved.base.pep440()})."
        )
    entries = entries_from_commits(since_final, requests)
    day = datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    name = tag_name(template, target)
    prefix = f"release({package})" if package else "release"
    return ReleasePlan(
        version=target,
        previous=resolved.base,
        tag=name,
        level=_level_text(resolved, explicit, chosen, source),
        section=render_section(
            target, entries, day=day, repo_url=github.repo_url(repo)
        ),
        files=_release_files(config, package),
        entries=entries,
        bump=resolved.plan,
        package=package,
        title=f"{prefix}: {name}",
        branch=f"{RELEASE_BRANCH}-{package}" if package else RELEASE_BRANCH,
    )

Without a version, HEAD must be the merged release commit, whose subject names the tag. With a version, HEAD is tagged by hand after the same checks.

:param config: The loaded configuration. :param version: Version to tag by hand. :param package: Package to tag instead of the repository. :param push: Push the tag to origin when that remote exists. :return: The tag name, the tagged commit and whether the tag was pushed. :raises CheckFailedError: If there is nothing to tag or the tag is not newer than the last release.

def tag_release(
    config: Config,
    *,
    version: str | None = None,
    package: str | None = None,
    push: bool = True,
) -> tuple[str, str, bool]:
    """
    Tag the release commit and push the tag.

    Without a version, ``HEAD`` must be the merged release commit, whose subject
    names the tag. With a version, ``HEAD`` is tagged by hand after the same
    checks.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param version: Version to tag by hand.
    :param package: Package to tag instead of the repository.
    :param push: Push the tag to ``origin`` when that remote exists.
    :return: The tag name, the tagged commit and whether the tag was pushed.
    :raises CheckFailedError: If there is nothing to tag or the tag is not newer
        than the last release.
    """
    repo = _require_repo(config)
    _require_own_tag(config, package)
    template, _scope = package_context(config, package)
    if version is not None:
        name = tag_name(template, Version.parse(version))
    else:
        found = _released_tag(repo, package)
        if found is None:
            raise CheckFailedError(
                "nothing to tag: HEAD is not a merged release pull request. "
                "Pass a VERSION to tag by hand."
            )
        name = found
    target = match_tag(template, name)
    if target is None:
        raise CheckFailedError(
            f"{name!r} does not follow the tag template {template!r}."
        )
    if name in repo.all_tags():
        raise CheckFailedError(f"tag {name} already exists.")
    existing = release_tags(template, repo.all_tags())
    if existing:
        latest = max(existing, key=lambda tag: existing[tag].sort_key())
        if target.sort_key() <= existing[latest].sort_key():
            raise CheckFailedError(f"{target.pep440()} is not newer than {latest}.")
    sha = repo.head() or ""
    if config.annotated:
        changelog = _changelog_path(config, package)
        message = (
            read_section(config.root / changelog, target) if changelog else None
        ) or name
        repo.git(
            *_identity(repo), "tag", "-a", name, "-m", message, "--cleanup=verbatim"
        )
    else:
        repo.git("tag", name)
    pushed = False
    if push and repo.git("remote", "get-url", "origin", check=False):
        repo.git("push", "-q", "origin", f"refs/tags/{name}")
        pushed = True
    else:
        logger.info("no origin remote; tag {} was created locally only", name)
    return name, sha, pushed

def write_release(config: Config, plan: ReleasePlan) -> list[str]:
    """
    Apply a plan to the working tree: changelog and committed targets.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param plan: The plan to apply.
    :return: Paths that changed, relative to the project root.
    """
    changed: list[str] = []
    changelog = _changelog_path(config, plan.package)
    if changelog:
        path = config.root / changelog
        old = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if path.is_file() else ""
        new = insert_section(old, plan.version, plan.section)
        if new != old:
            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
                handle.write(new)
            changed.append(changelog)
    resolved = Resolved(
        version=plan.version, type="release", source="release", tag=plan.tag
    )
    changes: list[Change] = stamp(
        config, resolved, package=plan.package, committed_only=True
    )
    changed += [change.path for change in changes if change.written]
    return changed

def match_tag(template: str, name: str) -> Version | None:
    """
    Read the version out of a tag name that follows a template.

    Both pre-release spellings are accepted, so ``v1.3.0-rc.1`` and ``v1.3.0rc1``
    give the same version.

    :param template: Tag template containing ``{version}``.
    :param name: Tag name to test.
    :return: The version, or ``None`` when the tag does not follow the template.
    """
    prefix, _, suffix = template.partition("{version}")
    if not name.startswith(prefix) or not name.endswith(suffix):
        return None
    body = name[len(prefix) : len(name) - len(suffix) if suffix else None]
    if not body or not body[0].isdigit():
        return None
    version = Version.try_parse(body)
    if version is None or version.dev is not None or version.local:
        return None
    return version

def resolve(
    config: Config,
    *,
    pin: str | None = None,
    build_type: BuildType | None = None,
    tag_template: str | None = None,
    path_scope: str | None = None,
) -> Resolved:
    """
    Resolve the version of the current checkout.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param pin: A version to use as is, skipping git.
    :param build_type: Force ``release``, ``dev`` or ``nightly``; by default a
        clean tagged ``HEAD`` is a release and anything else a development build.
    :param tag_template: Tag template to use instead of the configured one, for a
        package with its own tags.
    :param path_scope: Folder, relative to the project root, whose commits count;
        used for a package with its own tags.
    :return: The resolved version and how it was reached.
    :raises EnvironmentProblemError: In CI, when no trustworthy version exists.
    """
    template = tag_template or config.tag
    pinned = pin or (config.version if config.version != "auto" else None)
    if pinned:
        version = Version.parse(pinned)
        kind: BuildType = "release"
        if version.dev is not None:
            kind = "nightly" if version.nightly else "dev"
        return Resolved(
            version=version, type=kind, source="pin", notes=[f"pinned to {pinned}"]
        )

    warnings: list[str] = []
    fallback = Version.parse(config.fallback)
    repo = git.Repo.open(config.root)
    if repo is not None and repo.head() is None:
        repo = None
    if (
        repo is not None
        and (config.root / "PKG-INFO").is_file()
        and not repo.tracks(config.root)
    ):
        # An unpacked source distribution inside some other repository: the
        # surrounding history says nothing about this package.
        repo = None
    if repo is None:
        return _resolve_without_git(config, template, build_type, fallback, warnings)

    return _resolve_with_git(
        config,
        repo=repo,
        template=template,
        build_type=build_type,
        path_scope=path_scope,
        fallback=fallback,
        warnings=warnings,
    )

def scaffold(config: Config) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """
    Set up the files a repository needs for versions to survive without git.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :return: One ``(action, path, detail)`` row per step, where the action is
        ``wrote``, ``edit``, ``ok`` or ``todo`` for a change left to the user.
    """
    actions: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
    root = config.root
    archive = root / git.ARCHIVE_FILE
    if archive.is_file():
        actions.append(("ok", git.ARCHIVE_FILE, "already present"))
    else:
        archive.write_text(ARCHIVE_TEMPLATE, encoding="utf-8")
        actions.append(("wrote", git.ARCHIVE_FILE, ""))
    attributes = root / ".gitattributes"
    current = attributes.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if attributes.is_file() else ""
    if git.ARCHIVE_FILE in current and "export-subst" in current:
        actions.append(("ok", ".gitattributes", "already marks the archive file"))
    else:
        _append(attributes, _ATTRIBUTE_LINE)
        actions.append(("edit", ".gitattributes", f"+ {_ATTRIBUTE_LINE.strip()}"))
    pyproject = root / "pyproject.toml"
    if pyproject.is_file():
        text = pyproject.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        if (
            "hatchling" in text
            and "[tool.hatch.version]" not in text
            and "dynamic" in text
        ):
            _append(pyproject, '\n[tool.hatch.version]\nsource = "gitversioned"\n')
            actions.append(
                (
                    "edit",
                    "pyproject.toml",
                    '+ [tool.hatch.version] source = "gitversioned"',
                )
            )
        if not _requires_gitversioned(text):
            actions.append(
                (
                    "todo",
                    "pyproject.toml",
                    'add "gitversioned>=0.4" to [build-system] requires',
                )
            )
    return actions

@dataclass
class Target:
    """
    A file that carries the version.

    :param path: Absolute path of the file.
    :param kind: Handler name such as ``cargo``, ``npm`` or ``python``.
    :param standard: Spelling the file expects.
    :param commit: Whether the release pull request commits the file.
    :param locate: Finds the values to replace in the file's text.
    :param generated: True when the whole file is written from the template.
    """

    path: Path
    kind: str
    standard: Standard
    commit: bool
    locate: Callable[[str], list[Span]] = field(default=_no_spans, repr=False)
    generated: bool = False

    def current(self, text: str) -> str | None:
        """
        Read the version the file holds now.

        :param text: File content.
        :return: The first version value found, or ``None``.
        """
        for span in self.locate(text):
            if span.kind == "version":
                return text[span.start : span.end]
        return None

    def apply(self, text: str, values: dict[str, str]) -> str:
        """
        Replace each located value, leaving the rest of the text untouched.

        :param text: File content.
        :param values: Replacement per span kind.
        :return: The new content.
        """
        for span in sorted(
            self.locate(text), key=lambda item: item.start, reverse=True
        ):
            new = values.get(span.kind)
            if new is None:
                continue
            if span.kind == "req":
                operator = re.match(r"^[\^~=<>\s]*", text[span.start : span.end])
                new = (operator.group(0) if operator else "") + new
            text = text[: span.start] + new + text[span.end :]
        return text

def discover(config: Config, *, package: str | None = None) -> list[Target]:
    """
    Find every target of the project or of one package.

    Folders of packages that carry their own tag are left out of the repository's
    targets, and are the only folders searched when that package is asked for.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param package: Name of a package from ``[packages]`` to limit the search to.
    :return: The targets, discovered ones first, listed ones after.
    :raises ConfigError: If the package is unknown or a listed target is invalid.
    """
    base, excluded = _search_scope(config, package)
    paths = [
        path for path in _candidates(config, base) if _within(path, base, excluded)
    ]
    targets = _discovered(paths, base)
    for entry in config.targets:
        listed = _listed(config, entry)
        if not _within(listed.path, base, excluded):
            continue
        targets = [
            item for item in targets if item.path.resolve() != listed.path.resolve()
        ]
        targets.append(listed)
    return targets

def only_version_changed(
    config: Config,
    repo: git.Repo,
    path: str,
    known: list[Target] | None = None,
) -> bool:
    """
    Tell whether a dirty file differs from ``HEAD`` only by stamped values.

    This is what keeps a build from making its own tree dirty: a manifest whose
    only change is the version gitversioned wrote does not count.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param repo: The repository.
    :param path: Dirty path relative to the repository root.
    :param known: Targets already discovered, to avoid searching again per path.
    :return: True when the change is only gitversioned's own stamping.
    """
    absolute = (repo.top / path).resolve()
    try:
        targets = all_targets(config) if known is None else known
    except ConfigError:
        return False
    target = next((item for item in targets if item.path.resolve() == absolute), None)
    if target is None:
        return False
    if target.generated:
        return True
    head = repo.show(path)
    if head is None or not absolute.is_file():
        return False
    return _same_but_for_spans(target, head, _read_exact(absolute))

def python_module(pyproject: Path) -> Path | None:
    """Return where the generated ``version.py`` goes for a dynamic project."""
    try:
        data = tomllib.loads(pyproject.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError):
        return None
    project = data.get("project", {})
    build = data.get("build-system", {})
    uses_plugin = str(build.get("build-backend", "")).startswith("gitversioned") or any(
        re.match(r"^gitversioned\b", str(item).strip())
        for item in build.get("requires", [])
    )
    if not uses_plugin:
        return None
    if "version" not in project.get("dynamic", []) or not project.get("name"):
        return None
    package = re.sub(r"[-.]+", "_", str(project["name"])).lower()
    for base in (
        pyproject.parent / "src",
        pyproject.parent,
        pyproject.parent / "python",
    ):
        if (base / package).is_dir():
            return base / package / "version.py"
    return None

def render_version_module(resolved: Resolved) -> str:
    """
    Render the generated ``version.py`` for a resolved version.

    The module carries the version and git metadata only, so two builds of the
    same commit produce the same file.

    :param resolved: The resolved version.
    :return: Python source.
    """
    version = resolved.version
    parts: list[object] = [version.major, version.minor, version.patch]
    if version.pre is not None:
        parts.append(f"{version.pre[0]}{version.pre[1]}")
    if version.dev is not None:
        parts.append(f"dev{version.dev}")
    if version.local:
        parts.append(version.local)
    date = resolved.date.isoformat() if resolved.date else None
    return (
        '"""Version information generated by gitversioned. Do not edit or commit."""\n'
        "\n"
        "from __future__ import annotations\n"
        "\n"
        "__all__ = [\n"
        '    "__commit__",\n'
        '    "__commit_date__",\n'
        '    "__distance__",\n'
        '    "__tag__",\n'
        '    "__version__",\n'
        '    "__version_semver__",\n'
        '    "__version_tuple__",\n'
        '    "version",\n'
        '    "version_tuple",\n'
        "]\n"
        "\n"
        f"__version__ = version = {version.pep440()!r}\n"
        f"__version_semver__ = {version.semver()!r}\n"
        f"__version_tuple__ = version_tuple = {tuple(parts)!r}\n"
        f"__tag__ = {resolved.tag!r}\n"
        f"__distance__ = {resolved.distance!r}\n"
        f"__commit__ = {resolved.sha!r}\n"
        f"__commit_date__ = {date!r}\n"
    ).replace("'", '"')

def stamp(
    config: Config,
    resolved: Resolved,
    *,
    dry_run: bool = False,
    package: str | None = None,
    committed_only: bool = False,
    generated_only: bool = False,
) -> list[Change]:
    """
    Write the resolved version into every target.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param resolved: The version to write.
    :param dry_run: Compute the changes and diffs without touching any file.
    :param package: Limit the work to one package from ``[packages]``.
    :param committed_only: Skip targets the release pull request does not commit.
    :param generated_only: Write only the generated ``version.py`` files, as a
        build backend does.
    :return: One change per target, in discovery order.
    """
    changes: list[Change] = []
    for target in discover(config, package=package):
        if committed_only and not target.commit:
            continue
        if generated_only and not target.generated:
            continue
        relative = _relative(target.path, config.root)
        rendered = resolved.version.render(target.standard)
        old_text = _read_exact(target.path) if target.path.is_file() else ""
        if target.generated:
            old = _generated_version(old_text)
            new_text = render_version_module(resolved)
        else:
            old = target.current(old_text)
            new_text = target.apply(old_text, _values(target, resolved))
        diff = "".join(
            difflib.unified_diff(
                old_text.splitlines(keepends=True),
                new_text.splitlines(keepends=True),
                f"a/{relative}",
                f"b/{relative}",
            )
        )
        changed = new_text != old_text
        if changed and not dry_run:
            target.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with target.path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
                handle.write(new_text)
        changes.append(
            Change(
                relative, old, rendered, diff, target.commit, changed and not dry_run
            )
        )
    return changes

def build_package(config: Config, build_root: Path) -> str | None:
    """
    Name the ``[packages]`` entry a build folder belongs to, if any.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param build_root: Folder being built.
    :return: The package name, or ``None`` for the repository itself.
    """
    for name, item in config.packages.items():
        folder = (config.root / item.path).resolve()
        if build_root == folder or folder in build_root.parents:
            return name
    return None

Resolve the version for a build and write the generated module.

The build folder may sit below the project root, as an extra package under packages/<name>/ does: the version then follows that package's tags when it has its own, and only the build folder's own version.py is written.

:param root: Project folder being built. :param write: Write the generated version.py when the project has one. :return: The resolved version and the files written, relative to root.

Source code in src/gitversioned/plugins/__init__.py 
def resolve_for_build(
    root: Path | str, *, write: bool = True
) -> tuple[Resolved, list[Change]]:
    """
    Resolve the version for a build and write the generated module.

    The build folder may sit below the project root, as an extra package under
    ``packages/<name>/`` does: the version then follows that package's tags when
    it has its own, and only the build folder's own ``version.py`` is written.

    :param root: Project folder being built.
    :param write: Write the generated ``version.py`` when the project has one.
    :return: The resolved version and the files written, relative to ``root``.
    """
    build_root = Path(root).resolve()
    config = load_config(build_root)
    package = build_package(config, build_root)
    template, scope = package_context(config, package)
    resolved = resolve(config, tag_template=template, path_scope=scope)
    changes: list[Change] = []
    module = python_module(build_root / "pyproject.toml") if write else None
    if module is not None:
        text = render_version_module(resolved)
        old = module.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if module.is_file() else ""
        if old != text:
            module.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with module.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
                handle.write(text)
        changes.append(
            Change(
                path=module.relative_to(build_root).as_posix(),
                old=None,
                new=resolved.version.pep440(),
                diff="" if old == text else "changed",
                commit=False,
                written=old != text,
            )
        )
    return resolved, changes

class GitVersionedBuildHook(BuildHookInterface):
    """Ship the generated ``version.py`` even when git ignores it."""

    PLUGIN_NAME = "gitversioned"

    def initialize(self, version: str, build_data: dict[str, Any]) -> None:  # noqa: ARG002
        """
        Write the generated module and add it to the build as an artifact.

        :param version: Build version label passed by Hatchling.
        :param build_data: Mutable build data; ``artifacts`` is extended.
        """
        _resolved, changes = resolve_for_build(self.root)
        artifacts = build_data.setdefault("artifacts", [])
        for change in changes:
            if change.path not in artifacts:
                artifacts.append(change.path)

Stamp every target for the length of a build, then restore tracked files.

:param root: Project folder; defaults to the current one. :return: The resolved version in PEP 440 form.

@contextlib.contextmanager
def stamped(root: Path | None = None) -> Generator[str]:
    """
    Stamp every target for the length of a build, then restore tracked files.

    :param root: Project folder; defaults to the current one.
    :return: The resolved version in PEP 440 form.
    """
    build_root = (root or Path.cwd()).resolve()
    config = load_config(build_root)
    package = build_package(config, build_root)
    template, scope = package_context(config, package)
    resolved = resolve(config, tag_template=template, path_scope=scope)
    own_tag = package is not None and config.packages[package].tag is not None
    scoped = package if own_tag else None
    saved: dict[Path, str] = {}
    for target in discover(config, package=scoped):
        if not target.generated and target.path.is_file():
            with target.path.open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
                saved[target.path] = handle.read()
    stamp(config, resolved, package=scoped)
    try:
        yield resolved.version.pep440()
    finally:
        for path, text in saved.items():
            with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
                handle.write(text)
